title.zh: 卷二百九十二 列傳第五十一 李諮 程戡 夏侯嶠 盛度 丁度 張觀 鄭戩 明鎬 王堯臣 孫抃 田況
title.en: Volume 292 Biographies 51: Li Zi, Cheng Kan, Xia Houjiao, Cheng Du, Ding Du, Zhang Guan, Zheng Jian, Ming Gao, Wang Yaochen, Sun Bian, Tian Kuang
title.raw: 卷二百九十二 列傳第五十一 李諮 程戡 夏侯嶠 盛度 丁度 張觀 鄭戩 明鎬 王堯臣 孫抃 田況 Volume 292 Biographies 51: Li Zi, Cheng Kan, Xia Houjiao, Cheng Du, Ding Du, Zhang Guan, Zheng Jian, Ming Gao, Wang Yaochen, Sun Bian, Tian Kuang

sentences.zh: 李諮，字仲詢，唐趙國公峘之後。

translations.literal: Li Zi, style name Zhongxun, was a descendant of Han, Duke of Zhao of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zi, styled Zhongxun, traced his line to Han, the Tang-period Duke of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 峘貶死袁州，因家新喻，遂為新喻人。

translations.literal: Han was demoted and died at Yuanzhou; the family settled in Xinyu and thus became people of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: After Han was banished and died in Yuanzhou, the family made their home in Xinyu and became natives of that place.

sentences.zh: 諮幼有至性，父文捷出其母，諮日夜號泣，食飲不入口，父憐之而還其母，遂以孝聞。

translations.literal: From childhood Zi had supreme filial nature. His father Wen Jie sent his mother away; Zi wept day and night and would not eat or drink. His father took pity and restored his mother, and he became known for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Li Zi showed deep filial devotion. When his father Wen Jie sent his mother away, he wept day and night and refused food and drink until his father took pity and brought her back, and his filial fame spread.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，真宗顧左右曰：“是能安其親者。”

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination. Emperor Zhenzong looked to those around him and said: "This is one who can put his parents at ease."
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination. Emperor Zhenzong looked to those around him and said: "This is one who can put his parents at ease."

sentences.zh: 擢第三人，除大理評事、通判舒州，召試中書，為太子中允、直集賢院。

translations.literal: He was ranked third and appointed Reviewing Clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, concurrently Controller of Shuzhou, summoned for examination at the Secretariat, and made Crown Prince Attendant and Direct Academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents.
translations.idiomatic: He was placed third and appointed reviewing clerk of the Court of Judicial Review, concurrently controller of Shuzhou, summoned for examination at the Secretariat, and made crown prince attendant and direct academician of the Hall of Assembled Talents.

sentences.zh: 歷三司、開封府判官，再遷左正言，出為淮南轉運副使。

translations.literal: He served as judge of the Three Departments and Kaifeng Prefecture, was again promoted to Left Rectifying Censor, and went out as Vice Transport Commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: He served as judge of the Three Departments and Kaifeng Prefecture, was promoted again to left rectifying censor, and went out as vice transport commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 帝幸亳，以勞，遷尚書禮部員外郎。

translations.literal: When the emperor visited Bozhou, for his service he was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Bozhou, he was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Rites in the Secretariat in recognition of his service.

sentences.zh: 會江南饑，徙江東轉運副使，為度支判官。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan suffered famine, he was transferred to be Vice Transport Commissioner of Jiangdong and made Judge of the Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangnan suffered famine, he was transferred to vice transport commissioner of Jiangdong and made judge of the Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 擢知制誥，寇準數改諮所擬制辭，諮不樂，以父留鄉里請外，遂出知荊南。

translations.literal: Promoted to Drafting Edicts, Kou Zhun repeatedly revised the edicts Zi drafted; Zi was displeased and, because his father remained in the hometown, requested an outside post, and went out as Prefect of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to drafting edicts, Kou Zhun repeatedly revised the edicts Li Zi drafted. Displeased, and with his father still in the hometown, he requested an outside post and went out as prefect of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 會翰林學士闕，宰相擬他官，帝曰：“不如李諮。”

translations.literal: When a Hanlin Academician post fell vacant, the chief ministers proposed another official; the emperor said: "Li Zi would be better."
translations.idiomatic: When a Hanlin academician post fell vacant and the chief ministers proposed another official, the emperor said: "Li Zi would be better."

sentences.zh: 遂為學士。

translations.literal: He was then made an academician.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made an academician.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，超遷本曹郎中、權知開封府，數月，權三司使，拜右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was exceptionally promoted to Director of his bureau, acting Prefect of Kaifeng; within months he was acting Commissioner of the Three Departments, and appointed Right Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Renzong took the throne, he was exceptionally promoted to director of his bureau and acting prefect of Kaifeng; within months he was acting commissioner of the Three Departments and appointed right remonstrance censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏事兩宮曰：“天下賦調有定，今西北寢兵且二十年，而邊饋如故。

translations.literal: He once memorialized to the Two Palaces, saying: "The empire's tax levies are fixed; now the northwest has lain quiet from arms for nearly twenty years, yet frontier provisions remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: He once presented a memorial to the Two Palaces: "Nationwide taxes and levies are set, yet though the northwest has seen no major campaigning for nearly twenty years, border supplies are still funded at the old level.

sentences.zh: 戍兵雖未可滅，其末作浮費非本務者，宜一切裁損以厚下。”

translations.literal: Though garrison troops cannot yet be reduced, all secondary work, floating expenses, and matters not essential should be entirely cut to enrich those below."
translations.idiomatic: Garrison forces may not yet be cut, but every peripheral and wasteful expense outside core business should be trimmed wholesale so more reaches the common people."

sentences.zh: 即詔諮與御史中丞劉筠等同議冗費，以景德較天禧，計所減得十三之上。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was ordered together with Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jun and others to deliberate on redundant expenses; comparing the Jingde era with the Tianxi era, the calculated reduction attained above thirteen.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Li Zi, Vice Censor-in-Chief Liu Jun, and others jointly to review redundant spending; measured from Tianxi against Jingde, the reckoned savings came to more than thirteen parts per hundred.

sentences.zh: 時陜西緣邊數言軍食不給，度支都內錢不足支月奉，章獻太后憂之，命呂夷簡、魯宗道、張士遜與諮等經度其事。

translations.literal: At the time the Shaanxi frontier repeatedly reported insufficient military grain; the Finance Commission's pooled internal funds could not cover monthly salaries; Empress Dowager Zhangxian was troubled and ordered Lü Yijian, Lu Zongdao, Zhang Shixun, and Li Zi and others to survey and arrange the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile the Shaanxi borderlands kept reporting short military rations, and the Finance Commission's central reserves could not meet monthly pay; the Zhangxian Empress Dowager was alarmed and charged Lü Yijian, Lu Zongdao, Zhang Shixun, Li Zi, and others to overhaul the system.

sentences.zh: 諮曰：“舊法商人入粟邊郡，算茶與犀象、緡錢，為虛實三估，出錢十四文，坐得三司錢百文。”

translations.literal: Li Zi said: "Under the old law merchants delivered grain to border prefectures; tea was calculated together with rhinoceros horn, ivory, and strung cash as three assessments, nominal and real; putting out fourteen wen in cash, they could sit and obtain a hundred wen in the Three Departments' money."
translations.idiomatic: Li Zi said, "Under the old rules merchants brought grain into border prefectures; tea was calculated together with rhinoceros horn, ivory, and strung coin in a threefold nominal-and-real reckoning—paying fourteen cash in hand could secure a hundred cash worth from the Three Departments."

sentences.zh: 諮請變法以實錢入粟，實錢售茶，三者不得相為輕重。

translations.literal: Li Zi requested changing the law so that real cash entered for grain, real cash sold tea, and the three items might not be weighted against one another.
translations.idiomatic: He urged reform: grain paid in hard cash, tea sold for hard cash, with the three items barred from offsetting one another's value.

sentences.zh: 既行而商人果失厚利，怨謗蜂起。

translations.literal: Once implemented, the merchants truly lost their thick profits and complaints and slanders swarmed up.
translations.idiomatic: Once put in force the merchants truly lost their generous margin, and resentment and outcry spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 諮以疾累請郡，改樞密直學士、知洪州。

translations.literal: Li Zi, worn by illness repeatedly, requested a prefecture post; he was made Privy Council academician and prefect of Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zi, citing repeated illness, sought a provincial post and was made an academician of the Privy Council and prefect of Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 行數月，而御史臺鞫吏王舉、句獻私商人，多請慈州礬，會計茶法不折虛費錢，妄稱增課百萬緡，以覬恩賞。

translations.literal: Several months into his journey, the Censorate tried clerks Wang Ju and Gou Xian for privately favoring merchants, frequently requesting Cizhou alum; in accounting the tea law they did not discount nominal expense money but falsely claimed an increase in revenue of a million strings to court favor and reward.
translations.idiomatic: Months after he set out, the Censorate prosecuted clerks Wang Ju and Gou Xian for privately colluding with merchants—repeatedly requisitioning Cizhou alum—and in their tea-law accounts they refused to deduct fictitious expense cash yet falsely claimed a million strings in added revenue to win imperial favor.

sentences.zh: 諮坐不察奪職。

translations.literal: Li Zi was punished for failure to investigate and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zi was demoted for not having detected it.

sentences.zh: 久之，進給事中、知杭州，復樞密直學士、知永興軍。

translations.literal: After a long interval he was advanced to Supervising Censor and prefect of Hangzhou, then again Privy Council academician and commissioner of Yongxing Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he rose to Supervising Censor and prefect of Hangzhou, then again Privy Council academician and commissioner of Yongxing.

sentences.zh: 衣冠子弟恃蔭無賴者，諮悉杖之，境內肅然。

translations.literal: Sons of the gentry who relied on inherited privilege and were unruly—Li Zi had them all beaten with the staff, and within his jurisdiction all was orderly.
translations.idiomatic: He had every privileged scion who traded on hereditary standing and ran lawless beaten with the rod, and his jurisdiction became orderly.

sentences.zh: 還，勾當三班院，坐舉吏降左諫議大夫。

translations.literal: On return he managed the Three-Rank Court; for misconduct in recommending clerks he was demoted to Left Remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: When recalled he oversaw the Three-Rank Court; for faulty clerk recommendations he was reduced to Left Remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 權三司使事，是歲，禁中火，倉卒營造，應辦舉集。

translations.literal: Acting as Commissioner of the Three Departments that year, when fire broke out in the Forbidden precinct he urgently built and supplied everything needed was gathered.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Three Departments Commissioner that year, when fire broke out inside the palace compounds he rushed new construction and mustered every supply needed.

sentences.zh: 進尚書禮部侍郎，拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: Promoted Vice Minister of Rites of the Ministry of Rites and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted Vice Minister of Rites and appointed Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 數月，遭父喪，起復，遷戶部侍郎、知諫院事。

translations.literal: Several months later he suffered his father's mourning, was recalled from mourning, and moved to Vice Minister of Revenue and charged with Remonstrance Bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Months later his father died; recalled from mourning, he became Vice Minister of Revenue and head of remonstrance affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時榷茶法浸壞，乃詔諮、蔡齊等更議之。

translations.literal: At that time the government tea monopoly law was gradually breaking down; the court ordered Li Zi, Cai Qi, and others to revise it.
translations.idiomatic: The state tea monopoly was then decaying; the throne ordered Li Zi, Cai Qi, and others to revise it.

sentences.zh: 諮以前坐變法得罪，固辭，不許。

translations.literal: Li Zi, having before been punished for changing the law, firmly declined; the court would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zi, having once been faulted over his reform, steadfastly refused, but was not permitted to withdraw.

sentences.zh: 於是復用諮所變法，語具《食貨志》。

translations.literal: Thereupon they again employed the law Li Zi had changed; the details are given in full in the Monograph on Food and Goods.
translations.idiomatic: They then revived Li Zi's own reforms in full; particulars are set out in the Monograph on Food and Money.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈右僕射，謚憲成。

translations.literal: On death he was posthumously made Right Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat; canonized Xian-cheng.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously given Right Vice Director of the Secretariat, with the temple name Xiancheng.

sentences.zh: 諮性明辨，周知世務，其處煩猝，常若閑暇，吏不敢欺。

translations.literal: Li Zi's nature was clear and discriminating; he thoroughly knew affairs of the age; in handling urgency and sudden business he was ever as if at leisure, and clerks did not dare deceive him.
translations.idiomatic: Clear-eyed by nature and versed in worldly affairs, he handled rushing crises as if unhurried, and underlings did not dare cheat him.

sentences.zh: 在樞府，專務革濫賞，抑僥幸，人以為稱職。

translations.literal: In the Privy Council he devoted himself to reforming excessive rewards and checking improper favor; people considered him fitting the post.
translations.idiomatic: At the Privy Council he worked especially to cut bloated rewards and curb lucky petitions; colleagues judged him worthy of the role.

sentences.zh: 無子，以族子為後。

translations.literal: He had no son and adopted a clansman's child as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he took a kinsman's son as heir.

sentences.zh: 程戡，字勝之，許州陽翟人。

translations.literal: Cheng Kan, style name Shengzhi, was a native of Yangzhai in Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Kan, styled Shengzhi, came from Yangzhai in Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 少力學，舉進士甲科，補涇州觀察推官，再遷秘書丞、通判許州。

translations.literal: In youth he studied hard; passed the Presented Scholar examination in the top class; appointed investigating clerk of Jingzhou observation; twice promoted to Secretariat Director and prefectural vice commissioner of Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he studied strenuously, passed the jinshi in the top tier, served as an investigator under the Jingzhou intendant, and was twice promoted to Secretariat aide and vice prefect of Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 曹利用貶，戡以利用婿降通判蘄州。

translations.literal: When Cao Liyong was demoted, Kan as Liyong's son-in-law was reduced to vice commissioner of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Cao Liyong was banished, Kan—his son-in-law—was demoted to vice commissioner of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 徙虔州，州人有殺母，暮夜置屍仇人之門，以誣仇者。

translations.literal: Transferred to Qianzhou: a man in the prefecture killed his mother and at night placed the corpse at his enemy's gate to frame the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Qianzhou: a townsman murdered his mother and in the night laid the body at a foe's gate to incriminate him.

sentences.zh: 獄已具，戡獨辨之，正其罪。

translations.literal: The case was already complete, but Kan alone discerned the truth and fixed the proper guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The case was closed, yet Kan alone saw through it and assigned guilt correctly.

sentences.zh: 以尚書屯田員外郎知歸州，召為侍御史、三司度支判官。

translations.literal: As Vice Director of the Revenue section of the Ministry of Revenue he governed Guizhou; summoned as Attendant Censor and Finance Commission expenditure reviewer.
translations.idiomatic: As an assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue's granary section he governed Guizhou, then was summoned as Attendant Censor and expenditure reviewer of the Finance Commission.

sentences.zh: 寶元初，忻、代地震，壞城郭、廬舍，死傷甚眾，命戡安撫，頗以便宜從事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Baoyuan era Xin and Dai had earthquakes that ruined walled cities and houses with many dead and wounded; Kan was ordered to comfort and relieve and was broadly empowered to act as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Baoyuan, earthquakes in Xin and Dai wrecked cities and homes with heavy casualties; Kan was sent to console the region with broad discretion.

sentences.zh: 改起居舍人、知諫院，遷兵部員外郎兼侍御史知雜事、三司戶部副使。

translations.literal: Changed to Drafting Attendant and head of the Remonstrance Bureau; moved to Vice Director of the War Ministry concurrently Attendant Censor in charge of miscellaneous matters and War Section deputy of the Finance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He became Drafting Attendant and Remonstrance chief, then Vice Director of War while also Attendant Censor overseeing mixed business and deputy of the Finance Commission's households section.

sentences.zh: 擢天章閣待制、陜西都轉運使。

translations.literal: Raised to Hanlin academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion and Grand Transport Commissioner of Shaanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Elevated to academician of the Tianzhang Pavilion and grand transport commissioner for Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 未幾，知渭州。

translations.literal: Before long he was made prefect of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he governed Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 陜西有保毅軍，人苦其役。

translations.literal: Shaanxi had a Baoyi Army and the people suffered under its service.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi maintained a Baoyi militia, whose service duties oppressed the people.

sentences.zh: 戡奏曰：“保毅在鄉兵外，不黥而有籍，所以佐邊備也。

translations.literal: Kan memorialized: "The Baoyi stand outside the local militia, are not tattooed but carry registers, intended to assist border defense.
translations.idiomatic: Kan reported: "Baoyi troops sit outside the township militia—unbranded yet on the rolls—to reinforce frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 已隸保捷兵，而保毅籍如故，州縣以供力役，率困憊，至破析財產售田者，猶數戶出一夫，民不勝苦。”

translations.literal: They had already been enrolled in the Baojie Army yet the Baoyi registers remained as before; prefectures and counties drafted them for corvée and labor until exhausted, even to breaking up property and selling fields, still several households providing one man—the people could not bear the hardship."
translations.idiomatic: Though already listed with the Baojie Army, Baoyi registers stayed unchanged; districts still pressed them for labor until families were ruined—selling land and splitting estates—yet several households still owed one conscript; the burden was unbearable."

sentences.zh: 因詔：私役保毅者以計傭律坐之。

translations.literal: Therefore an edict: those who privately employed Baoyi were punished under the hired-labor statute.
translations.idiomatic: The court decreed that anyone who privately impressed Baoyi labor would be charged under the statute on hired labor.

sentences.zh: 進樞密直學士、知成都府。

translations.literal: Advanced to Privy Council academician and prefect of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced to Privy Council academician and prefect of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 坐嘗保任貝州張得一，得一伏誅，奪職出知鳳翔府，尋徙河中。

translations.literal: Because he had once guaranteed Zhang Deyi of Beizhou, and Deyi was executed on confession, his office was stripped and he went out as prefect of Fengxiang; soon transferred to Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He had vouched for Beizhou's Zhang Deyi; when Deyi was put to death after confessing, Kan lost his post and was sent out to Fengxiang, then soon to Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞張觀辨之，復為樞密直學士、知永興軍，徙瀛州，四遷給事中。

translations.literal: Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Guan cleared him; restored as Privy Council academician and commissioner of Yongxing; moved to Yingzhou; four promotions to Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhang Guan vindicated him; he returned as Privy Council academician and Yongxing commissioner, then Yingzhou, and after four steps reached Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 契丹使過，稱疾，求著帽見，戡使謂曰：“有疾，可毋相見，見當如禮。”

translations.literal: When a Khitan envoy passed through he claimed illness and asked to be received wearing a cap; Kan's envoy told him: "If ill, you need not meet at all; if you meet, you must follow ritual."
translations.idiomatic: A Liao envoy passing through pleaded illness and asked to be received capped rather than bare-headed; Kan's deputy told him, "If you are ill you need not appear at all—but if you appear you follow protocol."

sentences.zh: 使者語屈，冠而見。

translations.literal: The envoy's words were bent and he met wearing his cap.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy yielded and met with his cap on.

sentences.zh: 人言歲在甲午蜀且有變，孟知祥之割據，李順之起而為盜，皆此時也。

translations.literal: People said that in a jiawu year Shu would have upheaval—Meng Zhixiang's secession and Li Shun rising as bandit both occurred in such years.
translations.idiomatic: Folk omens held that in a jiawu year Shu would see turmoil: Meng Zhixiang's breakaway and Li Shun's bandit uprising had both happened then.

sentences.zh: 仁宗自擇戡再知益州，遷端明殿學士，召見慰遣。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong himself chose Kan to govern Yizhou again; promoted to Duanming Hall academician; summoned and consoled on departure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong personally reappointed Kan to Yizhou, made him Duanming Hall academician, summoned him, and sent him off with reassurance.

sentences.zh: 至彭州，民妄言有兵變，捕斬之。

translations.literal: Reaching Pengzhou, the people falsely rumored military mutiny; he arrested and beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: At Pengzhou commoners spread false talk of troop mutiny; he seized and executed them.

sentences.zh: 守益州者以嫌，多不治城堞，戡獨完城浚池自固，不以為嫌也。

translations.literal: Those guarding Yizhou out of suspicion often did not repair ramparts; Kan alone completed walls and dredged moats to secure himself, not treating it as suspicion.
translations.idiomatic: Previous Yizhou governors, fearing suspicion, often let battlements go; Kan alone repaired walls and deepened moats without caring that it might look suspicious.

sentences.zh: 召拜參知政事，奏禁蜀人妖言誣民者。

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Vice Grand Councilor; memorialized to forbid Shu people's demon talk that misled the people.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled as Vice Councilor, he petitioned to outlaw Sichuan demagogues who deceived the populace.

sentences.zh: 避宰相文彥博親，改尚書戶部侍郎、樞密副使。

translations.literal: To avoid kinship with Grand Councilor Wen Yanbo he was changed to Vice Minister of Revenue of the Revenue Ministry and Vice Commissioner of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: To avoid clashing with Grand Councilor Wen Yanbo's family ties, he became Revenue Vice Minister and Privy Council vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 數與宋庠爭議，諫官、御史皆論之，戡亦自請罷。

translations.literal: He repeatedly disputed with Song Qi; remonstrators and censors all criticized this; Kan also asked to resign.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled often with Song Qi; remonstrators and censors rebuked them both, and Kan himself asked to step down.

sentences.zh: 除吏部侍郎、觀文殿學士兼翰林侍讀學士、同群牧制置使，尋拜宣徽南院使、鄜延路經略安撫使、判延州。

translations.literal: Made Vice Minister of Personnel, academician of the Observant Culture Hall and Hanlin Reader-in-Waiting, co-director of the Imperial Herd; soon appointed Southern Bureau Commissioner of the Imperial Insignia, Commissioner-in-Chief of Frontier Pacification and Comfort of the Fuyan Route, and acting prefect of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed Personnel Vice Minister, Observant Culture academician and Hanlin reader-in-waiting, co-administrator of the imperial stud; soon Southern Hall commissioner of the imperial insignia, Fuyan route pacification commissioner, and acting Yanzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，以安武軍節度使留再任。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yingzong succeeded the throne he was retained as Military Commissioner of Anwu with a second term.
translations.idiomatic: At Yingzong's accession he was kept on as Anwu military commissioner for another term.

sentences.zh: 初，覃恩，蕃官例不序遷。

translations.literal: At first under grace amnesties frontier officials by precedent did not advance in rank.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier tribal officers had not, by custom, received seniority promotions on general amnesties.

sentences.zh: 至是，用戡奏始皆得遷。

translations.literal: Now on Kan's memorial they all received promotion.
translations.idiomatic: On Kan's petition they now all gained promotions.

sentences.zh: 又請首領有戰功材武，皆得召見，選補為蕃官。

translations.literal: He also asked that leaders with battle merit and martial talent all be summoned and selected to fill tribal posts.
translations.idiomatic: He further asked that any chieftain with battlefield merit and martial ability be called in and posted as frontier tribal officer.

sentences.zh: 延州夾河為兩城，雉堞頗卑小。

translations.literal: Yanzhou straddled the river as two cities and its battlements were quite low.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhou sat on both banks as twin cities with rather low parapets.

sentences.zh: 敵登九州臺，則下瞰城中。

translations.literal: If the enemy climbed Jiuzhou Terrace they could look down into the city.
translations.idiomatic: From Jiuzhou Terrace the enemy could overlook the town below.

sentences.zh: 戡調兵夫大增築之。

translations.literal: Kan mobilized laborers and greatly added to the fortifications.
translations.idiomatic: Kan drafted laborers and greatly enlarged the defenses.

sentences.zh: 橫山酋豪怨諒祚，欲率其屬叛，取靈、夏，來求兵為援。

translations.literal: Chiefs of the Hengshan tribes resented Liang Zuo and wished to lead their followers in rebellion to take Ling and Xia, coming to request troops in aid.
translations.idiomatic: Hengshan chieftains, angered at Liang You, meant to rebel and seize Ling and Xia, and came seeking Song troops.

sentences.zh: 戡言：“豺虎非自相搏，則未易取也；

translations.literal: Kan said: "Wolves and tigers do not easily fall unless they fight each other;
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "Jackals and tigers are not easily taken unless they tear at one another;

sentences.zh: 癰疽非其自潰，則未易攻也。

translations.literal: an abscess is not easily attacked unless it bursts of itself.
translations.idiomatic: nor is a carbuncle easily struck until it ruptures on its own.

sentences.zh: 諒祚久悖慢，宜乘此許之，所謂以蠻夷攻蠻夷，中國之利也。”

translations.literal: Liang Zuo has long been arrogant—this is the time to promise them; it is the so-called using barbarians to attack barbarians, profit for the Middle Kingdom."
translations.idiomatic: Liang You's insolence has lasted long—now is the moment to agree; this is letting barbarians fight barbarians, to China's advantage."

sentences.zh: 會英宗不豫，大臣重生事，不報。

translations.literal: But as Emperor Yingzong fell ill the great ministers feared fresh troubles and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: But Yingzong fell ill and senior ministers feared new entanglements, so nothing was answered.

sentences.zh: 言者請選大臣帥永興，屯重兵以制五路，敕戡具利害以聞。

translations.literal: Critics asked that a high minister command Yongxing and station heavy troops to control the five routes; the throne ordered Kan to report advantages and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Memorialists proposed a senior commander at Yongxing with heavy troops to oversee five frontier circuits; Kan was told to weigh costs and benefits.

sentences.zh: 戡以為“四路距永興皆十數驛，設有警，使聽節制，則不及事矣。

translations.literal: Kan held that "the four routes are all a dozen or more post-stages from Yongxing; if alarm came and they awaited orders, it would be too late for events.
translations.idiomatic: Kan argued that "each of the four circuits lies many stages from Yongxing—if trouble arose and all waited on central orders, events would outrun response.

sentences.zh: 且關中財賦不贍，宿軍多，何以給之？”

translations.literal: Moreover Guanzhong's wealth could not support it; many troops already garrisoned there—how provide for more?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Guanzhong's revenues cannot sustain more—troops already encamped there in numbers—how feed another host?"

sentences.zh: 治平初，命宦官王昭明等領四路蕃部事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhiping era eunuchs Wang Zhaoming and others were put in charge of tribal affairs on the four routes.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhiping eunuchs including Wang Zhaoming were assigned to lead tribal affairs on all four frontier circuits.

sentences.zh: 戡曰：“蕃部所以亡去，苦邊吏苛暴，為西人誘略爾。

translations.literal: Kan said: "Tribes left because frontier officials were harsh and violent and Western people lured and enticed them.
translations.idiomatic: Kan said, "Tribes have defected because border clerks were brutal and Westerners seduced them.

sentences.zh: 今昭明等徒能呼召首領，犒以牛酒，恐未足以結其心也。

translations.literal: Now Zhaoming and others can only summon leaders and regale them with cattle wine—I fear that is not enough to win their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhaoming and his kind can only summon chiefs and toast them with cattle and wine—hardly enough to bind loyalty.

sentences.zh: 而甚動邊聽，宜更置路分鈐轄、都監，各部一將兵，兼沿邊巡檢使，無復專蕃部事。”

translations.literal: Yet they greatly stir border rumor; it would be better to place route branch controllers and chief inspectors, one general each with patrol authority along the border, and no longer concentrate solely on tribal business."
translations.idiomatic: They also stir frontier gossip; better to install route deputies and chief inspectors, each circuit with one field commander doubling as border patrol commissioner, and end exclusive eunuch control of tribal affairs."

sentences.zh: 從其奏。

translations.literal: The memorial was adopted.
translations.idiomatic: The throne accepted his plan.

sentences.zh: 夏人遣使入貢，僣漢官移文於州，稱其國中官曰樞密。

translations.literal: Western Xia sent envoys to offer tribute, falsely using Han-style documents to prefectures calling their officials "Privy Council."
translations.idiomatic: Xi Xia envoys came to pay tribute but used Han-style notes to prefectures, styling their countryman as "Privy Councilor."

sentences.zh: 戡止令稱使副不以官，稱樞密曰“領廬”，方許之。

translations.literal: Kan stopped them, ordering them to call the envoy and deputy without office titles; only when "Privy Council" was rendered as "leading the lodges" would he permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Kan barred it, allowing only envoy and deputy without ranks, and only if "Privy Councilor" became "head of the official residence."

sentences.zh: 戡告老章累上，終弗聽，遣使以手詔問勞，賜茶藥、黃金，乃再上章曰：“臣老疾劇矣，高奴屯勁兵為要地，豈養病所耶？”

translations.literal: Kan repeatedly memorialized to retire but was never heeded; the court sent envoys with an autograph edict to inquire after him and bestow tea, medicine, and gold; he memorialized again: "My old illness is severe; Gaonu stations crack troops at a key point—how is that a place to nurse sickness?"
translations.idiomatic: Kan filed many retirement pleas without answer; the throne sent messengers with an autograph to console him and grant tea, medicines, and gold; he wrote again: "My ailments are grave—is Gaonu, where elite troops guard a choke point, a sickroom?"

sentences.zh: 召還，道卒。

translations.literal: Recalled on the road he died.
translations.idiomatic: Called back, he died on the journey.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，謚康穆。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Marshal; canonized Kang-mu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Grand Marshal, temple name Kangmu.

sentences.zh: 戡久在邊，安重習事，治不近名。

translations.literal: Kan long served on the frontier, steady and practiced in affairs, governing without seeking fame.
translations.idiomatic: Long on the border, steady and seasoned, he ruled without courting renown.

sentences.zh: 然不為言者所與，或傳戡交通宦官閻士良，至令妻出見之。

translations.literal: Yet he did not win the support of critics; some spread that Kan trafficked with eunuch Yan Shiliang, even making his wife come out to meet him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet critics never took his side; rumor said he dealt with eunuch Yan Shiliang—even made his wife appear to receive him.

sentences.zh: 夏侯嶠

translations.literal: Xia Houjiao
translations.idiomatic: Xia Houjiao

sentences.zh: 夏侯嶠，字峻極，其先幽州人。

translations.literal: Xia Houjiao, style name Junji, his ancestors were people of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xia Houjiao, styled Junji, was of Youzhou stock.

sentences.zh: 高祖秀，為濟州鉅野鎮遊奕使，因家焉。

translations.literal: His ancestor Xiu in Gaozu's time was roaming patrol officer of Juye Town in Jizhou and settled the family there.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Xiu, under Gaozu, served as roving patrol officer of Juye post in Jizhou and made the locale his home.

sentences.zh: 父浦，梁開平中，以明經至棣州錄事參軍。

translations.literal: His father Pu in Kaiping of Later Liang by the Classical Learning examination reached Recorder of Di Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Father Pu, in Later Liang's Kaiping era, reached Di prefecture recorder via the Mingjing exam.

sentences.zh: 嶠幼好學，弱冠，以辭賦稱，周相李谷延置門下。

translations.literal: Jiao from youth loved learning; in weak cap years he was famed for rhapsody and verse; Zhou Chancellor Li Gu extended invitation and kept him at his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao studied avidly as a boy; by his twenties he was known for fu and verse; Zhou minister Li Gu brought him into his household.

sentences.zh: 又依西京留守向拱，攝伊陽令；

translations.literal: He also relied on Western Capital garrison commissioner Xiang Gong; acted as magistrate of Yiyang;
translations.idiomatic: He served under Luoyang garrison commissioner Xiang Gong as acting magistrate of Yiyang;

sentences.zh: 拱移安州，又令攝錄事參軍。

translations.literal: when Gong moved to Anzhou he again had Jiao act as recorder.
translations.idiomatic: when Gong moved to Anzhou, Jiao again acted as recorder.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，舉進士甲科，解褐大理評事、通判興州，累遷右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping xingguo he passed Presented Scholar in the top class, left office as Grand Court reviewer and vice commissioner of Xingzhou, and was repeatedly promoted to Right Assistant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In early Taiping xingguo he took jinshi in the top tier, began as Grand Court reviewer and vice commissioner of Xingzhou, and rose to Right Assistant Censor.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，督芻糧於河朔。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Taiyuan he supervised forage in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan expedition he oversaw fodder in Hebei.

sentences.zh: 遷殿中丞、通判邠州。

translations.literal: Promoted to Palace Director and vice commissioner of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Palace Director and vice commissioner of Bin.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，拜監察御史、通判興元府，進秩殿中。

translations.literal: When his term ended he was appointed Investigating Censor and vice commissioner of Xingyuan Prefecture, with rank advanced in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: At term's end he became Investigating Censor and vice commissioner of Xingyuan, advancing one grade in the palace service.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年代還，對便殿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi when his replacement term ended he was received in the side hall.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxi year two, when his term ended, Taizong received him in the side hall.

sentences.zh: 太宗語有司曰：“此人朕自知其才行，勿須奏擬。”

translations.literal: Taizong told the officials: "This man's talent and conduct I know myself; need not submit for deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: Taizong said to the staff, "I myself know this man's talent and conduct—do not route a nomination memorandum."

sentences.zh: 即日改左補闕、直史館，賜緋魚。

translations.literal: That same day he was made Left Supplementation Censor and straight historian of the Historiography Office, granted crimson robe and fish tally.
translations.idiomatic: That day he became Left Supplementation Censor and direct historian, with crimson robe and fish tally.

sentences.zh: 會王師護邊，乘傳督河間餫道，就命知莫州。

translations.literal: When imperial armies guarded the frontier he went by express to supervise Hejian supply roads and was then appointed prefect of Mo.
translations.idiomatic: As imperial forces guarded the borders he rode express to supervise Hejian grain routes and was appointed Mo prefect on the spot.

sentences.zh: 逾月，徙洪州，改起居郎。

translations.literal: After a month transferred to Hongzhou; changed to Drafting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: A month later moved to Hongzhou; made Drafting Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 真宗在襄邸，太宗擇朝士謹厚者為官屬，即召入為翊善，賜金紫，加直昭文館。

translations.literal: When the true heir was at Xiang mansion Taizong chose meticulous court gentlemen as staff; he was summoned as Tutor and given gold and purple rank, added as straight historian of the Zhaowen Hall.
translations.idiomatic: While Prince Zhenzong was at his Xiang residence, Taizong chose sober courtiers as staff and summoned Jiao as tutor, granting gold-purple rank and making him straight historian of Zhaowen Hall.

sentences.zh: 真宗尹京府，命兼推官，加司封員外郎。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong governed the capital prefecture he was ordered also as sheriff-reviewer and added Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhenzong administered the capital prefecture Jiao was also made reviewing sheriff and added Chief Clerk of the Revenue Section.

sentences.zh: 東宮建，復兼中舍，遷工部郎中。

translations.literal: When the Eastern Palace was founded he again served as Central Drafting Attendant and was moved to Director of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: With establishment of the Eastern Palace he doubled as Central Drafting Attendant and rose to Director of Works.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，拜給事中、知審刑院。

translations.literal: When the heir succeeded he was appointed Supervising Censor and head of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At accession he was made Supervising Censor and director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 數月，擢樞密院副使。

translations.literal: After several months, he was promoted Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later he was made vice commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 咸平元年，以戶部郎中罷。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianping he was dismissed while Director in the Revenue Section of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Xianping year one he left office as Revenue-section director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 二年，始建講讀之職，命嶠為翰林侍讀學士。

translations.literal: In the second year the lecture-and-reading posts were first established, and Jiao was appointed Hanlin Attendant Reader academician.
translations.idiomatic: Year two the court created lecture-and-reading posts and named Jiao Hanlin Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 及楊徽之卒，又命兼秘書監。

translations.literal: When Yang Huizhi died, he was also ordered to serve concurrently as Director of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Huizhi died he was also made concurrent Director of the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 是秋，江、浙饑，命為江南巡撫使，所過疏理刑訟，存問耆老，務從寬簡，人以為便。

translations.literal: That autumn Jiang and Zhe suffered famine; he was appointed Jiangnan touring pacification commissioner. Wherever he passed he cleared and settled criminal cases, inquired after the aged, and strove for leniency and simplicity; people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn famine struck Jiang and Zhe; appointed Jiangnan touring commissioner, he cleared lawsuits, visited the elderly, and favored lenient, simple handling—people welcomed it.

sentences.zh: 使還，采病民二十餘事上之，亟詔厘革。

translations.literal: When the mission returned he collected more than twenty matters harming the people and submitted them; the court urgently ordered rectification.
translations.idiomatic: Back from the tour he reported twenty-odd abuses harming commoners; the throne quickly ordered reforms.

sentences.zh: 又判吏部選事。

translations.literal: He also served as acting director of Ministry of Personnel selections.
translations.idiomatic: He also oversaw Ministry of Personnel selections.

sentences.zh: 嶠善鼓琴，好讀莊、老書，淳厚謹慎，居官無過失。

translations.literal: Jiao was skilled at the zither, loved reading Zhuangzi and Laozi, was pure, thick, and cautious, and in office committed no faults.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao played the zither well, read Zhuangzi and Laozi, and was steady and careful—never faulted in office.

sentences.zh: 真宗尤愛重之，多所詢訪，每以善人目之。

translations.literal: Zhenzong especially cherished him, often sought his counsel, and always regarded him as a good man.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong prized him, consulted him often, and always called him a man of virtue.

sentences.zh: 素好道，留意養生，少疾。

translations.literal: He had long favored the Way, attended to nurturing life, and seldom fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: Long devoted to the Way and regimen, he rarely fell ill.

sentences.zh: 景德元年五月，以選人俟對崇政殿，暴中風眩，亟詔取金丹，上尊酒餌之，肩輿還第，遣內侍召外內名醫診視。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the first year of Jingde, while waiting at Chongzheng Hall as a selection candidate, he suddenly suffered wind dizziness; the court urgently ordered golden elixir brought and imperial wine given him; he was carried by sedan chair back to his residence, and inner attendants were sent to summon famous physicians within and without the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Jingde year one, fifth month: awaiting audience at Chongzheng Hall as a selection candidate, he collapsed with apoplexy; the court sent for golden elixir and imperial wine, had him borne home in a sedan, and dispatched inner attendants to summon renowned physicians.

sentences.zh: 其夕卒，年七十二。

translations.literal: That evening he died, aged seventy-two.
translations.idiomatic: He died that night at seventy-two.

sentences.zh: 詔贈兵部尚書，賵賜外，增賜白金三百兩給葬。

translations.literal: An edict posthumously made him Minister of War; beyond funeral gifts, three hundred taels of white gold were added for burial.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously made Minister of War; beyond standard funeral gifts, three hundred taels of white gold were granted for burial.

sentences.zh: 錄其子大理寺丞晟為太子中舍，孫恭為奉禮郎，侄孫蔚賜同學究出身。

translations.literal: His son Sheng, Registrar of the Court of Judicial Review, was enrolled as Central Drafting Attendant of the Heir Apparent; his grandson Gong made Court Gentleman for Offering; his grand-nephew Wei was granted the same origin as a fellow student.
translations.idiomatic: Son Sheng, Court of Judicial Review registrar, was made Heir Apparent Central Drafting Attendant; grandson Gong, Court Gentleman for Offering; grand-nephew Wei granted fellow-student origin.

sentences.zh: 嶠在近侍，恩遇甚渥。

translations.literal: Jiao among close attendants received very generous favor.
translations.idiomatic: As a close attendant Jiao enjoyed exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 卒後數月，畢士安為相，撫坐嘆曰：“使夏侯君在，吾豈先據此位！”

translations.literal: Several months after his death Bi Shian became chief minister; stroking his seat he sighed: "Had Lord Xia Hou been alive, how could I have taken this post first!"
translations.idiomatic: Months after his death Bi Shian became chief minister and, patting his seat, sighed: "If Lord Xiahou still lived, how could I have sat here first!"

sentences.zh: 有集十五卷。

translations.literal: He left a collection in fifteen juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left a fifteen-juan collection.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符初，晟上《漢武封禪圖》，繢金匱、玉匱、石<石感>、石距之狀，鹹有註釋，上覽而善之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong xiangfu, Sheng submitted "Diagram of Han Wu's Feng and Shan," painting forms of the gold casket, jade casket, stone shi-gan, and stone ju, all annotated; the emperor viewed it and approved.
translations.idiomatic: Early Dazhong xiangfu Sheng presented "Diagram of Han Wu's Feng and Shan," illustrating gold and jade caskets and ceremonial stone forms with full notes; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 至駕部員外郎。

translations.literal: He rose to Vice Director of the Transport Section.
translations.idiomatic: He reached Vice Director of the Transport Section.

sentences.zh: 恭至太子中舍。

translations.literal: Gong rose to Central Drafting Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Gong rose to Heir Apparent Central Drafting Attendant.

sentences.zh: 盛度，字公量，世居應天府，後徙杭州余杭縣。

translations.literal: Sheng Du, style name Gongliang, for generations dwelt in Yingtian Prefecture, later moved to Yuhang County, Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Du, styled Gongliang, was long settled in Yingtian Prefecture, later moved to Yuhang in Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 曾祖珰，仕錢氏為余杭縣令。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Dang served the Qian clan as magistrate of Yuhang.
translations.idiomatic: Great-grandfather Dang served the Qian house as Yuhang magistrate.

sentences.zh: 父豫，從錢俶入朝，終尚書度支郎中。

translations.literal: His father Yu followed Qian Chu to court and ended as Director of the Revenue Section in the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Father Yu followed Qian Chu to court and died Revenue-section director in the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 度舉進士第，補濟陰尉。

translations.literal: Du passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Jiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Du passed the jinshi and was made Jiyin assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 選為封丘主簿，改府倉曹參軍，為光祿寺丞、御史臺推勘官，改秘書省秘書郎。

translations.literal: Selected as registrar of Fengqiu, changed to granary staff officer of the prefecture, served as Vice Director of the Imperial Household Administration and investigating officer of the Censorate, then changed to Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Made Fengqiu registrar, then prefectural granary officer, Imperial Household vice director and Censorate investigator, then Palace Library secretary.

sentences.zh: 試學士院，為直史館、三司戶部判官，累遷尚書屯田員外郎。

translations.literal: He passed the Hanlin examination, became straight historian of the Historiography Office and Revenue-section judge of the Three Departments, and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the State Farms Section.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the Hanlin exam he became Historiography Office straight historian and Three Departments revenue judge, rising to State Farms vice director.

sentences.zh: 契丹寇邊，從幸大名，數上疏論邊事。

translations.literal: When the Khitan raided the frontier he followed the emperor to Daming and repeatedly submitted memorials on border affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan raided the border he accompanied the emperor to Daming and memorialized repeatedly on frontier policy.

sentences.zh: 奉使陜西，因覽疆域，參質漢、唐故地，繪為《西域圖》以獻。

translations.literal: On mission to Shaanxi he surveyed the territory, compared it with Han and Tang former lands, and painted a "Western Regions Map" to present.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to Shaanxi he surveyed the region against Han and Tang holdings and presented a "Western Regions Map."

sentences.zh: 改開封府判官，坐決獄失實，降監洪州稅。

translations.literal: Changed to judge of the Kaifeng prefecture; for deciding cases untruthfully he was demoted to supervisor of Hongzhou tax.
translations.idiomatic: Made Kaifeng judge; untruthful verdicts demoted him to Hongzhou tax supervisor.

sentences.zh: 起知建昌軍、三司鹽鐵判官，改起居舍人、知制誥。

translations.literal: He was raised to prefect of Jianchang Army and salt-and-iron judge of the Three Departments, then Drafting Gentleman and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Restored as Jianchang prefect and Three Departments salt-and-iron judge, then Drafting Gentleman and edict drafter.

sentences.zh: 度嘗奏事便殿，真宗問其所上《西域圖》，度因言：“酒泉、張掖、武威、敦煌、金城五郡之東南，自秦築長城，西起臨洮，東至遼碣，延袤萬里。

translations.literal: Du once memorialized in the side hall; Zhenzong asked about his submitted "Western Regions Map," and Du said: "Southeast of the five commanderies Jiuquan, Zhangye, Wuwei, Dunhuang, and Jincheng—from when Qin built the Long Wall west from Lintao east to Liaojie, extending ten thousand li.
translations.idiomatic: Memorializing in the side hall, Zhenzong asked about his "Western Regions Map"; Du said: "Southeast of Jiuquan, Zhangye, Wuwei, Dunhuang, and Jincheng—from Qin's Long Wall west at Lintao east to Liaojie, ten thousand li.

sentences.zh: 有郡、有軍、有守捉，襟帶相屬，烽火相望，其為形勢備禦之道至矣。

translations.literal: There were commanderies, armies, and garrison commands, linked like a collar and belt, beacon fires in sight of one another—the formation and means of defense were complete.
translations.idiomatic: Commanderies, armies, and garrisons linked like a belt, beacons in sight—the defensive layout was complete.

sentences.zh: 唐始置節度，後以宰相兼領，用非其人，故有河山之險而不能固，有甲兵之利而不能禦。

translations.literal: Tang first established military commissioners, later had chief ministers concurrently hold them; employing unfit men, therefore though they had river-and-mountain barriers they could not hold firm, though they had armor and troops they could not defend.
translations.idiomatic: Tang created commissioners, later filled by chief ministers with unfit men—hence barriers and arms alike failed.

sentences.zh: 今復繪山川、道路、壁壘、區聚，為《河西隴右圖》，願備上覽。”

translations.literal: Now I have again painted mountains, rivers, roads, ramparts, and settlements as "Hexi Longyou Map," wishing it be prepared for Your Majesty's viewing."
translations.idiomatic: Now I have redrawn terrain, roads, walls, and settlements as "Hexi Longyou Map" for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 真宗稱其博學。

translations.literal: Zhenzong praised his erudition.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong praised his learning.

sentences.zh: 後遷右諫議大夫、權知開封府。

translations.literal: Later promoted Right Remonstrance Censor and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Later Right Remonstrance Censor and acting Kaifeng prefect.

sentences.zh: 以疾不拜，改會靈觀判官，入翰林為學士，加史館修撰。

translations.literal: Because of illness he did not accept; changed to judge of the Hall of Numinous Communion, entered the Hanlin as academician, and added Historiography Office reviser.
translations.idiomatic: Illness kept him from accepting; made Hall of Numinous Communion judge, Hanlin academician, Historiography reviser.

sentences.zh: 歷兵部郎中、景靈宮副使。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the War Section and deputy commissioner of the Palace of Brilliant Numen.
translations.idiomatic: Served War Section director and Brilliant Numen deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 寇準罷相，度以交通周懷政，出知光州。

translations.literal: When Kou Zhun was dismissed as chief minister, Du for associating with Zhou Huaizheng was sent out as prefect of Guang.
translations.idiomatic: When Kou Zhun fell, Du's tie to Zhou Huaizheng sent him out as Guang prefect.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，再謫和州團練副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing he was again demoted to military training vice commissioner of He.
translations.idiomatic: Early Qianxing he was again demoted to He military training vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁謂貶，起為祠部郎中，復兵部郎中，遷太常少卿、知筠州，更虔、滁、蘇三州。

translations.literal: When Ding Wei was demoted he was raised as Director of the Rites Section, restored War Section director, promoted Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Administration and prefect of Yun, then changed through Qian, Chu, and Su prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding Wei fell he was raised Rites Section director, restored War Section director, made Imperial Sacrifices vice director and Yun prefect, then Qian, Chu, and Su.

sentences.zh: 還知審刑院，以右諫議大夫知揚州，加集賢院學士。

translations.literal: On return he headed the Court of Judicial Review, as Right Remonstrance Censor governed Yangzhou, and was added academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Back he headed Judicial Review, governed Yangzhou as Right Remonstrance Censor, and joined the Hall of Assembled Worthies.

sentences.zh: 初，度謫洪州，建請復賢良方正科，又請建四科以取士，曰：博通墳典達於教化科，才識兼茂明於體用科，軍謀宏遠堪任將帥科，明曉法律能按章覆問科。

translations.literal: Earlier when Du was demoted to Hongzhou he memorialized to restore the "worthy and upright" examination and to establish four categories for selecting scholars, namely: thorough mastery of canonical texts reaching to transformation and teaching; talent and insight together with clarity in institutional application; grand military counsel fit to command generals; and clarity in law able to review cases by statute.
translations.idiomatic: Demoted to Hongzhou he urged restoring the worthy-and-upright exam and four talent categories: canonical mastery for teaching, talent with institutional insight, military counsel for command, legal clarity for case review.

sentences.zh: 既而用夏竦議，置六科，其議亦自度始。

translations.literal: Later following Xia Song's proposal six categories were established—the proposal also began with Du.
translations.idiomatic: Later six categories were set on Xia Song's motion—Du had originated the idea.

sentences.zh: 復為翰林學士、史館修撰，遷給事中。

translations.literal: Restored as Hanlin academician and Historiography reviser, promoted Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Restored Hanlin academician and Historiography reviser, promoted Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 嘗受詔與御史中丞王隨議通解鹽，聽商旅入錢算鹽，語在《食貨志》。

translations.literal: He once received orders with Vice Censor-in-Chief Wang Sui to discuss liberalizing salt transport, allowing merchants to pay cash for salt allotments—the account is in the "Food and Goods Treatise."
translations.idiomatic: Ordered with Vice Censor Wang Sui to liberalize salt, letting merchants pay cash for allotments—see the Food and Goods Treatise.

sentences.zh: 尋進承旨，以禮部侍郎兼端明殿學士，召問邊計，退而條十事上之。

translations.literal: Soon advanced to chief academician, as Vice Minister of Rites concurrently academician of the Illustrious Hall, summoned to discuss border plans; on withdrawal he listed ten items and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon chief Hanlin academician, Vice Rites Minister and Illustrious Hall academician; questioned on borders, he submitted ten points.

sentences.zh: 又兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently as Attendant Reader academician.
translations.idiomatic: He also doubled as Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 景祐二年，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jingyou he was appointed Vice Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyou year two he became Vice Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 時王曾、呂夷簡為相，度與宋綬、蔡齊並參知政事，曾與齊善，而夷簡與綬善，惟度不得志於二人。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Zeng and Lü Yijian were chief ministers; Du with Song Shou and Cai Qi were all vice participants; Zeng was friendly with Qi while Yijian was friendly with Shou—only Du could not realize his aims with the two.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zeng and Lü Yijian were chief ministers; Du, Song Shou, and Cai Qi were vice participants; Zeng favored Qi, Yijian favored Shou—Du satisfied neither pair.

sentences.zh: 及二人俱辭相，仁宗問度曰：“王曾、呂夷簡力求退，何也？”

translations.literal: When both men together resigned as chief minister, Renzong asked Du: "Wang Zeng and Lü Yijian strive to retire—why?"
translations.idiomatic: When both resigned, Renzong asked Du why Wang Zeng and Lü Yijian pressed to leave.

sentences.zh: 度對曰：“二人腹心之事，臣不得而知，陛下詢二人以孰可代者，則其情可察矣。”

translations.literal: Du replied: "The inner matters of the two men your servant cannot know; if Your Majesty asks each whom he would replace them with, then their feelings can be discerned."
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "I cannot know their private motives; ask each whom he would name as successor and their intent will show."

sentences.zh: 仁宗果以問曾，曾薦齊，又問夷簡，夷簡薦綬，於是四人俱罷，而度獨留。

translations.literal: Renzong indeed asked Zeng; Zeng recommended Qi; he also asked Yijian; Yijian recommended Shou—thereupon all four were dismissed while Du alone remained.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong asked Zeng, who named Qi; asked Yijian, who named Shou—all four left, Du alone stayed.

sentences.zh: 遷知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Promoted to head the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was made head of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 章得象既相，以度嘗位其上，即拜武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dexiang had become chief minister, because Du had once ranked above him, he was immediately appointed military commissioner of Wuning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Dexiang as chief minister, Du having once outranked him, was sent out as Wuning military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 坐令開封府吏馮士元強取其鄰所賃官舍，以尚書右丞罷。

translations.literal: For letting Kaifeng clerk Feng Shiyuan forcibly take his neighbor's rented official residence he was dismissed as Right Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He fell as Right Secretariat vice director for letting Kaifeng clerk Feng Shiyuan seize a neighbor's leased official quarters.

sentences.zh: 復知揚州，加資政殿學士、知應天府。

translations.literal: Restored as Yangzhou prefect, added academician of the Hall of Assisting Governance and prefect of Yingtian.
translations.idiomatic: Restored Yangzhou prefect, added Assisting Governance academician and Yingtian prefect.

sentences.zh: 暴感風眩，以太子少傅致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Suddenly stricken with wind dizziness, he retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: Struck by apoplexy, he retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Wensu.

sentences.zh: 度好學，家居列圖書，每歸，未嘗釋手。

translations.literal: Du loved learning; at home he arrayed books and whenever he returned never released them from his hand.
translations.idiomatic: A devoted reader, he lined his home with books and never set them down when home.

sentences.zh: 敏於為文，而泛濫不精。

translations.literal: He was quick at composition but diffuse and not refined.
translations.idiomatic: Quick with prose but diffuse and unpolished.

sentences.zh: 嘗奉詔同編《續通典》、《文苑英華》，註釋御集。

translations.literal: He once received orders jointly to compile "Continuation of the Comprehensive Institutions," "Finest Blossoms of the Literary Garden," and annotate the imperial collected works.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to help compile Continuation of the Comprehensive Institutions and Finest Blossoms and annotate imperial collections.

sentences.zh: 真宗祀汾陰，仁宗在藩邸，詔掌起居箋奏及留司章奏。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong sacrificed at Fenyin, Renzong was in the princely residence; he was ordered to manage memorials of daily record and memorials left with the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenzong's Fenyin sacrifice, with Renzong in the princely residence, he handled daily-record and capital memorials.

sentences.zh: 有《愚谷》、《銀臺》、《中書》、《樞中》四集，又有《中書》、《翰林》二制集。

translations.literal: He had four collections "Fool's Valley," "Silver Terrace," "Central Secretariat," and "Bureau of Military Affairs," and also two edict collections for the Central Secretariat and Hanlin.
translations.idiomatic: His collections Fool's Valley, Silver Terrace, Central Secretariat, and Bureau of Military Affairs, plus two edict volumes for Secretariat and Hanlin.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年，詔許中書舍人、給事中、諫議大夫母封郡太君，而學士不預。

translations.literal: In the third year of Tianxi an edict allowed mothers of Secretariat drafting attendants, supervising censors, and remonstrance censors to be enfeoffed as Grand Lady of a commandery, but academicians were not included.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi year three edict enfeoffed mothers of drafting attendants, supervising censors, and remonstrance censors as commandery grand ladies—but not Hanlin academicians.

sentences.zh: 時度官兵部郎中，因請追封其母，自是學士官未至諫議者，其母皆得封郡君。

translations.literal: At the time Du was acting War Section director; he requested posthumous enfeoffment for his mother—thereafter mothers of academicians not yet remonstrance censors could all be enfeoffed as commandery ladies.
translations.idiomatic: As acting War Section director he sought posthumous enfeoffment for his mother; thereafter Hanlin mothers below remonstrance rank could be enfeoffed commandery ladies.

sentences.zh: 度體肥大，艱於拜起，賓客有拜之者，則俯伏不能興，往往瞪視而詬詈之。

translations.literal: Du's body was large and stout; bowing and rising were difficult for him. When guests bowed to him he would bend low and could not rise, often staring and reviling them.
translations.idiomatic: Corpulent, he struggled to bow; when guests bowed he stayed bent, unable to rise, and often glared and cursed them.

sentences.zh: 性極猜險，雖平居，僚友不敢易語言。

translations.literal: His nature was extremely suspicious and dangerous; even in ordinary times colleagues dared not speak casually with him.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply suspicious, colleagues scarcely dared casual speech even in private.

sentences.zh: 所至，下貧無賴，多所縱舍；

translations.literal: Wherever he went, the destitute and lawless he often indulged;
translations.idiomatic: Where he governed he often indulged the destitute and lawless;

sentences.zh: 稍有貲者，一切繩之以法。

translations.literal: whoever had any property at all he bound entirely with the law.
translations.idiomatic: anyone with property he prosecuted to the letter.

sentences.zh: 子申甫，終尚書兵部郎中、集賢校理，嘗為福建轉運使，頗以修潔稱。

translations.literal: His son Shenfu ended as War Section director in the Ministry of War and collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies; he once was Fujian transport commissioner and was quite praised for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Son Shenfu died War Section director and Hall collator; once Fujian transport commissioner, noted for integrity.

sentences.zh: 從兄京，有吏能，以尚書工部侍郎致仕，卒。

translations.literal: His cousin Jing had administrative talent; he retired as Vice Minister of Works in the Ministry of Works and died.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Jing, capable in administration, retired as Works vice minister and died.

sentences.zh: 丁度，字公雅，其先恩州清河人。

translations.literal: Ding Du, style name Gongya, his ancestors were people of Qinghe in En Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Du, styled Gongya, came from Qinghe in En Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖顗，後唐清泰初陷契丹，逃歸，徙居祥符。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yan in the beginning of Qingtai of Later Tang fell to the Khitan, escaped back, and moved to Xiangfu.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Yan, early Later Tang Qingtai, was taken by Khitan, escaped, and settled at Xiangfu.

sentences.zh: 父逢吉，以醫術事真宗藩邸，然好聚書，與儒者遊。

translations.literal: His father Fengji practiced medicine in Zhenzong's princely residence, yet loved gathering books and associated with Confucians.
translations.idiomatic: Father Fengji practiced medicine in Zhenzong's princely household yet collected books and mingled with scholars.

sentences.zh: 度強力學問，好讀《尚書》，尚擬為《書命》十餘篇。

translations.literal: Du studied with force, loved reading the "Documents," and once drafted more than ten chapters in imitation of "Charges."
translations.idiomatic: Du studied hard, loved the Documents, and drafted ten-odd chapters modeled on Charges.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符中，登服勤詞學科，為大理評事、通判通州，改太子中允、直集賢院。

translations.literal: In Dazhong xiangfu he passed the "diligent in service and literary learning" examination, was made reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review and vice commissioner of Tongzhou, changed to Central Drafting Attendant of the Heir Apparent and straight collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Dazhong xiangfu he passed the diligent-service literary exam, made Judicial Review reviewer and Tong vice commissioner, then Heir Apparent Central Drafting Attendant and Hall collator.

sentences.zh: 坐解送國子監進士失實，監齊州稅。

translations.literal: For escorting National University jinshi with untruthful records he was demoted to supervisor of Qi Prefecture tax.
translations.idiomatic: Untruthful jinshi escort records demoted him to Qi tax supervisor.

sentences.zh: 還知太常禮院，判吏部南曹。

translations.literal: On return he knew the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and judged the southern desk of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Restored he ran Imperial Sacrifices and judged Personnel's southern desk.

sentences.zh: 上書論六事：一、增講讀官；

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial discussing six matters: first, increase lecture-and-reading officials;
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized six points: first, add lecture-and-reading officers;

sentences.zh: 二、增諫員；

translations.literal: second, increase remonstrance officials;
translations.idiomatic: second, add remonstrance officers;

sentences.zh: 三、補蔭用大功以上親；

translations.literal: third, extend yin privilege to relatives within great-gong mourning;
translations.idiomatic: third, extend yin privilege to great-gong kin;

sentences.zh: 四、選河北、河東役兵補禁軍；

translations.literal: fourth, select corvée soldiers from Hebei and Hedong to replenish the forbidden army;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, draft Hebei and Hedong corvée troops into the forbidden army;

sentences.zh: 五、籍令佐墾田為殿最；

translations.literal: fifth, register assistant magistrates' reclaimed fields for merit ratings;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, score magistrates' assistants by reclaimed land;

sentences.zh: 六、凡緣公事坐私罪仗者，聽保任遷官。

translations.literal: sixth, all who for public matters receive private flogging punishments may be guaranteed for transfer.
translations.idiomatic: sixth, allow guarantors for officials flogged for private offenses tied to public duty.

sentences.zh: 章獻太后善之。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager Zhangxian approved.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager Zhangxian approved.

sentences.zh: 舊制，監司及藩鎮辭謁皆賜對。

translations.literal: By old regulation, when circuit commissioners and frontier commissioners took leave to pay respects they were all granted audience.
translations.idiomatic: Old rules granted audience when circuit and frontier commissioners took leave to pay respects.

sentences.zh: 仁宗初即位，止令附中書、樞密奏之，度言，附奏非所以防壅蔽也。

translations.literal: When Renzong first acceded he ordered only attachment to the Central Secretariat and Bureau of Military Affairs memorials; Du said attachment was not the way to guard against obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: At Renzong's accession memorials went only through Secretariat and Military Affairs; Du said that invited obstruction.

sentences.zh: 又嘗獻《王鳳論》於章獻太后，以戒外戚。

translations.literal: He also once presented "Discourse on Wang Feng" to Empress Dowager Zhangxian to warn against maternal kin.
translations.idiomatic: He also gave Empress Dowager Zhangxian "Discourse on Wang Feng" to warn against consort kin.

sentences.zh: 歷三司磨勘司、京西轉運使。

translations.literal: He served as auditor of the Three Departments, Western Capital transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He audited the Three Departments and served Western Capital transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 司天言永昌陵有白氣，請增築以厭之，有詔按視。

translations.literal: The Directorate of Astronomy said there was white vapor at Yongchang Tomb and requested added construction to suppress it; there was an edict to inspect.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomers reported white vapor at Yongchang Tomb and sought added works to suppress it; the court ordered inspection.

sentences.zh: 度奏神道貴靜，不可輕繕治，乃止。

translations.literal: Du memorialized that the spirit way values stillness and must not be lightly repaired, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Du said the spirit way should stay quiet and works ceased.

sentences.zh: 入知制誥，遷翰林學士，糾察在京刑獄，判太常禮院兼群牧使。

translations.literal: He entered as drafter of edicts, was promoted Hanlin academician, investigated capital criminal cases, and judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices while concurrently commissioner of the Herds.
translations.idiomatic: Made edict drafter, Hanlin academician, capital criminal investigator, Imperial Sacrifices judge and Herds commissioner.

sentences.zh: 劉平、石元孫敗，帝遣使問所以禦邊。

translations.literal: When Liu Ping and Shi Yuan sun were defeated the emperor sent envoys to ask how to defend the border.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were defeated the emperor asked how to defend the frontier.

sentences.zh: 度奏曰：“今士氣傷沮，若復追窮巢穴，饋糧千里，輕用人命以快一朝之意，非計之得也。

translations.literal: Du memorialized: "Now morale is wounded and depressed; if we again pursue the enemy to their lair, supply grain a thousand li, and lightly spend lives to satisfy a moment's wish, it is not a winning plan.
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "Morale is shattered; to chase the enemy deep, supply grain a thousand li, and spend lives for a moment's satisfaction is no winning plan.

sentences.zh: 唐都長安，天寶後，河、湟覆沒，涇州西門不開，京師距寇境不及五百里，屯重兵，嚴烽火，雖常有侵軼，然卒無事。

translations.literal: Tang made Chang'an its capital; after Tianbao, He and Huang were overrun, Jing Prefecture's western gate did not open, the capital was not five hundred li from the enemy border, yet heavy troops were stationed, beacons were strict—though there were often raids, in the end there was no major trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Tang held Chang'an; after Tianbao He-Huang fell, Jing's west gate stayed shut, the capital within five hundred li of enemies—yet heavy garrisons and beacons kept raids from becoming disaster.

sentences.zh: 太祖時，疆場之任，不用節將。

translations.literal: In Taizu's time frontier duty did not use military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Under Taizu frontiers did not use military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 但審擢材器，豐其廩賜，信其賞罰，方陲輯寧幾二十年。

translations.literal: Only carefully select talent and capacity, enrich their grain stipends, trust their rewards and punishments—the borders were tranquil for nearly twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: He chose talent, enriched stipends, trusted rewards and punishments—borders stayed quiet nearly twenty years.

sentences.zh: 為今之策，莫若謹亭障，遠斥堠，控扼要害，為制禦之全計。”

translations.literal: For present policy, nothing surpasses carefully maintaining pavilions and barriers, distant scouts, controlling strategic points—a complete plan of defense and control."
translations.idiomatic: Today's policy: maintain barriers, distant scouts, hold key points—a full defensive plan."

sentences.zh: 因條上十策，名曰《備邊要覽》。

translations.literal: Thereupon he listed ten policies, titled "Essentials for Border Defense."
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted ten policies titled Essentials for Border Defense.

sentences.zh: 時西疆未寧，二府三司，雖旬休不廢務。

translations.literal: At the time the western frontier was not yet settled; the two bureaus and three departments, though on ten-day rest, did not cease business.
translations.idiomatic: The west was still unsettled; the two bureaus and three departments kept working even on rest days.

sentences.zh: 度言：“苻堅以百萬師寇晉，謝安命駕出遊以安人心。

translations.literal: Du said: "Fu Jian with a million troops invaded Jin; Xie An ordered his carriage out to tour and settle people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "When Fu Jian invaded Jin with a million men, Xie An went out touring to steady hearts.

sentences.zh: 請給假如故，無使外夷窺朝廷淺深。”

translations.literal: I request granting leave as of old, lest outer barbarians spy the court's depth or shallowness."
translations.idiomatic: Grant leave as before, lest foreigners gauge the court's strength."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The court followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人，為承旨。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Secretariat drafting attendant and made chief academician.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Secretariat drafting attendant, then chief academician.

sentences.zh: 時葉清臣請商州置監鑄大錢，以一當十。

translations.literal: At the time Ye Qingchen requested Shang Prefecture establish a mint to cast large coins worth ten each.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Qingchen sought a Shang mint casting ten-for-one large coins.

sentences.zh: 度奏曰：“漢之五銖，唐之開元及國朝錢法，輕重大小，最為折中。

translations.literal: Du memorialized: "Han's five zhu, Tang's Kaiyuan, and our dynasty's coin law in light and heavy, large and small, are most balanced.
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "Han five-zhu, Tang Kaiyuan, and our coin law strike the best balance of weight and size.

sentences.zh: 歷代改更，法雖精密，不能期年，即復改鑄。

translations.literal: Through the ages when laws were changed, though the statutes were refined, within a year they would cast anew.
translations.idiomatic: Each dynasty's refinements could not hold a year before recoining.

sentences.zh: 議者欲繩以峻法，革其盜鑄。

translations.literal: Planners wished to bind with harsh law and end illicit casting.
translations.idiomatic: Reformers wanted harsh laws to stop illicit casting.

sentences.zh: 昔漢變錢幣，盜鑄死者數十萬。

translations.literal: Formerly when Han changed currency, those executed for illicit casting numbered hundreds of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Han's currency change brought hundreds of thousands of casting executions.

sentences.zh: 唐鑄乾元及重輪乾元錢，錢輕幣重，嚴刑不能禁止。

translations.literal: Tang cast Qianyuan and double-ring Qianyuan coins; money was light and goods heavy—severe punishments could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Tang's Qianyuan coins made money light and goods heavy; harsh law failed.

sentences.zh: 今禁旅戍邊，月給百錢，得大錢裁十，不可畸用，舊錢不出，新錢愈輕，則芻糧增價。

translations.literal: Now garrison troops on the frontier receive a hundred coins monthly; large coins yield only ten—unusable alone; old coins do not circulate, new coins grow lighter, and fodder prices rise.
translations.idiomatic: Frontier troops get a hundred small coins monthly—only ten large ones, unusable alone; old coin hoarded, new coin debased, fodder prices climb.

sentences.zh: 臣嘗知湖州，民有抵茶禁者，受千錢立契代鞭背。

translations.literal: Your servant once governed Huzhou: one who violated the tea ban took a thousand coins to contract a flogging on the back.
translations.idiomatic: In Huzhou I saw tea-ban violators pay a thousand coins to take lashes by contract.

sentences.zh: 在京西，有強盜殺人，取其弊衣，直不過數百錢。

translations.literal: In Jingxi a robber killed a man for worn clothes worth only a few hundred coins.
translations.idiomatic: In Jingxi a robber killed for rags worth hundreds of coins.

sentences.zh: 盜鑄之利，不啻數倍。

translations.literal: Profit from illicit casting is not merely several times greater.
translations.idiomatic: Illicit casting profits many times over.

sentences.zh: 復有湖山絕處，兇魁嘯聚，爐冶日滋，居則鑄錢，急則為盜。

translations.literal: Again in remote lakes and mountains fierce leaders gather; furnaces daily increase—at ease they cast coin, in urgency they become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Remote hills harbor chiefs who cast by day and rob when pressed.

sentences.zh: 民間銅鉛之器，悉為大錢，何以禁止。”

translations.literal: Household bronze and lead vessels would all become large coins—how could it be forbidden?"
translations.idiomatic: Household bronze and lead would become large coin—how forbid it?"

sentences.zh: 度又言：“祥符、天聖間，牧馬至十餘萬，其後言者以天下無事，不可虛費，遂廢八監。

translations.literal: Du also said: "In Xiangfu and Tiansheng times pasture horses reached more than a hundred thousand; later speakers said the realm was at peace and such expense was empty, and eight pasturage offices were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Du also said: "Xiangfu-Tiansheng herds topped a hundred thousand; peace advocates abolished eight pasturage offices as waste.

sentences.zh: 然猶秦渭環階麟府文州、火山保德岢嵐軍，歲市馬二萬二百匹，補京畿、塞下之闕。

translations.literal: Yet Qin, Wei, Huan, Jie, Lin, Fu, Wenshan, Huoshan, Baode, and Kelan armies still yearly bought twenty-two thousand horses to fill gaps in the capital region and border garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: Yet border markets still bought twenty-two thousand horses yearly for capital and frontier shortfalls.

sentences.zh: 自西鄙用兵，四年所牧，三萬而已。

translations.literal: Since western campaigns, in four years only thirty thousand were raised.
translations.idiomatic: Four years of western war raised only thirty thousand.

sentences.zh: 馬少地閑，坊監誠可罷；

translations.literal: Horses few and land idle—pasturage offices truly may be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: With few horses and idle land, pasturage offices may close;

sentences.zh: 若賊平馬歸，則不可闕。

translations.literal: if bandits are pacified and horses return, they cannot be lacking.
translations.idiomatic: but when peace returns horses cannot be wanting.

sentences.zh: 今河北、河東、京東西、淮南皆籍丁壯為兵，請令民畜一戰馬者，得免二丁，仍不許貲產以升戶等，則緩急有備，而國馬蕃矣。”

translations.literal: Now Hebei, Hedong, eastern and western Jingdong, and Huainan all register able-bodied men as soldiers; I request that one who keeps a war horse be exempt two corvée laborers and still not be allowed to use property to raise household rank—then in urgency there is preparation and state horses multiply."
translations.idiomatic: Let a household keeping a war horse exempt two corvée men without buying rank—urgent need met, state herds grow."

sentences.zh: 慶歷中，副杜衍宣撫河東。

translations.literal: In Qingli he served as deputy to Du Yan pacifying Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Qingli he deputized Du Yan pacifying Hedong.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷端明殿學士、知審刑院。

translations.literal: After long service promoted Illustrious Hall academician and head of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Later Illustrious Hall academician and Judicial Review head.

sentences.zh: 時江西轉運使移屬州，凡市米鹽鈔，每百緡貼納錢三之一。

translations.literal: At the time the Jiangxi transport commissioner shifted subordinate prefectures: for every hundred strings of rice, salt, or salt certificates, one-third was added as surcharge.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxi transport made subordinates add one-third surcharge per hundred strings on rice, salt, or certificates.

sentences.zh: 通判吉州李虞卿受財免貼納，事覺，大理將以枉法論。

translations.literal: Jizhou vice prefect Li Yuqing took bribes to waive surcharge; the matter was exposed and the Court of Judicial Review would judge by bending the law.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou vice prefect Li Yuqing took bribes to waive surcharge; Judicial Review sought a bending-law verdict.

sentences.zh: 度曰：“枉法，謂於典憲有所阿曲。

translations.literal: Du said: "Bending the law means curving canonical statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "Bending the law means distorting canonical statutes.

sentences.zh: 虞卿所違者，轉運使移文爾。”

translations.literal: What Yuqing violated was only the transport commissioner's dispatch."
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing violated only a transport dispatch."

sentences.zh: 遂貸虞卿死。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yuqing's death sentence was commuted.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing's death sentence was commuted.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗問，用人以資與才孰先？

translations.literal: The emperor once asked whether in employing men seniority or talent comes first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked whether seniority or talent should come first in appointments.

sentences.zh: 度對曰：“承平時用資，邊事未平宜用才。”

translations.literal: Du replied: "In peaceful times use seniority; while border affairs are unsettled talent should be used."
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "Use seniority in peace, talent while borders are unsettled."

sentences.zh: 時度在翰林已七年，而朝廷方用兵，故對以此。

translations.literal: At the time Du had been in the Hanlin seven years while the court was campaigning, hence he answered thus.
translations.idiomatic: He had served Hanlin seven years amid war, hence the answer.

sentences.zh: 諫官孫甫論度所言，蓋自求柄用，帝諭輔臣曰：“度在侍從十五年，數論天下事，顧未嘗及私，甫安從得是語。”

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Sun Fu criticized Du's words as seeking power for himself; the emperor told chief ministers: "Du has been in attendance fifteen years, often discussing realm affairs, yet never touched private interest—how could Fu get such words?"
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Sun Fu criticized Du's words as seeking power for himself; the emperor told the chief ministers: "Du has been in attendance fifteen years, often discussing realm affairs, yet never touched private interest—how could Fu get such words?"

sentences.zh: 未幾，擢工部侍郎、樞密副使。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted Vice Minister of Works and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Vice Works Minister and Military Affairs vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 因言：“周世宗募驍健，有朝出群盜、夕備宿衛者；

translations.literal: He said: "Later Zhou Shizong recruited the valiant; some who were bandits by morning were palace guards by evening;
translations.idiomatic: He said: "Zhou Shizong recruited braves—bandits by morning, guards by evening;

sentences.zh: 太祖閱猛士實騎軍。
