translations.literal: Taizu reviewed fierce warriors to fill the cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu reviewed warriors to fill the cavalry.

sentences.zh: 請擇河北、河東、陜西就糧馬軍，以補禁旅之闕。”

translations.literal: I request selecting grain-fed horse armies of Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi to fill gaps in the forbidden army."
translations.idiomatic: Select Hebei, Hedong, and Shaanxi grain-fed horse troops to fill forbidden-army gaps."

sentences.zh: 又言：“契丹嘗渝盟，預備不可忽。”

translations.literal: He also said: "The Khitan once broke the covenant—preparation must not be neglected."
translations.idiomatic: He warned Khitan covenant-breaking demanded vigilance.

sentences.zh: 因上《慶歷兵錄》五卷、《贍邊錄》一卷。

translations.literal: Thereupon he submitted five juan of 《Qingli Military Records》 and one juan of 《Frontier Provisioning Records》.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted five juan of 《Qingli Military Records》 and one of 《Frontier Provisioning Records》.

sentences.zh: 明年，參知政事。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Vice Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Next year he became Vice Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 會春旱，降秩中書舍人，逾月，復官。

translations.literal: When spring drought occurred his rank was lowered to Secretariat drafting attendant; after a month his office was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Spring drought lowered him to drafting attendant; a month later restored.

sentences.zh: 後二年，衛士為變，事連宦官楊懷敏，樞密使夏竦請御史與宦官同於禁中鞫之，不可滋蔓，令反側者不自安。

translations.literal: Two years later palace guards mutinied, the affair involving eunuch Yang Huaimin; Military Affairs Commissioner Xia Song requested censors and eunuchs jointly interrogate within the palace lest it spread and unsettle those wavering.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later guards mutinied, implicating eunuch Yang Huaimin; Xia Song wanted censors and eunuchs to interrogate inside the palace.

sentences.zh: 度曰：“宿衛有變，事關社稷，此而可忍孰不可忍！

translations.literal: Du said: "When palace guards change, it concerns the altars of soil and grain—if this can be borne, what cannot be borne!
translations.idiomatic: Du said: "A guard mutiny touches the altars—if this is borne, what is not?

sentences.zh: 請付外臺窮治黨與。”

translations.literal: I request handing to outer offices to exhaustively try the clique."
translations.idiomatic: Hand it to outer offices to try the clique thoroughly."

sentences.zh: 爭於帝前。

translations.literal: They argued before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: They argued before the throne.

sentences.zh: 仁宗從竦言，度遂求解政事，罷為紫宸殿學士兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Renzong followed Xia Song; Du then requested release from governance and was dismissed as Purple Hall academician with Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong sided with Xia Song; Du left governance for Purple Hall academician with Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 御史何郯言，紫宸非官稱所宜。

translations.literal: Censor He Zan said Purple Hall was not a proper title designation.
translations.idiomatic: Censor He Zan said Purple Hall was not a proper title.

sentences.zh: 改觀文殿學士、知通進銀臺司、判尚書都省，再遷尚書左丞，卒。

translations.literal: Changed to Observant Culture Hall academician, head of the Silver Terrace Memorial Office, and director of the Secretariat Chancery; again promoted Left Vice Director of the Secretariat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Made Observant Culture academician, Silver Terrace head, Secretariat Chancery director, then Left Secretariat vice director and died.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚文簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of Personnel, posthumous title Wenjian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Personnel Minister, posthumous Wenjian.

sentences.zh: 度性淳質，不為威儀，居一室十余年，左右無姬侍。

translations.literal: Du's nature was pure and plain, without imposing ceremony; he dwelt in one room more than ten years with no concubines at his side.
translations.idiomatic: Plain and unceremonious, he lived one room over ten years without concubines.

sentences.zh: 然喜論事，在經筵歲久，帝每以學士呼之而不名。

translations.literal: Yet he loved discussing affairs; long in the classics hall, the emperor often called him "academician" without his name.
translations.idiomatic: He loved debate; long in the classics hall the emperor called him "academician" without name.

sentences.zh: 嘗問蓍龜占應之事，乃對：“卜筮雖聖人所為，要之一技而已，不若以古之治亂為監。”

translations.literal: He was once asked about divination with yarrow and tortoise responses and replied: "Though divination was made by sages, after all it is but one craft—better take ancient order and disorder as mirror."
translations.idiomatic: Asked about yarrow and tortoise divination he said it was but a craft—better mirror on past order and chaos.

sentences.zh: 又嘗示以欹器曰：“朕欲臨天下以中正之道。”

translations.literal: He was also once shown a tilted vessel and said: "I wish to face the realm with the way of centrality and correctness."
translations.idiomatic: Shown a tilted vessel the emperor said he wished to rule by centrality.

sentences.zh: 度對曰：“臣等亦願無傾滿以事陛下。”

translations.literal: Du replied: "Your servants also wish no tipping or overflowing in serving Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: Du said servants too wished no tipping or overflowing in serving him.

sentences.zh: 因奏太宗嘗作此器，真宗亦嘗著論，於是帝制《後述》以賜之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that Taizong once made this vessel and Zhenzong also wrote a discourse; thereupon the emperor composed 《Later Discourse》 to grant him.
translations.idiomatic: He noted Taizong and Zhenzong had written on the vessel; the emperor composed 《Later Discourse》 for him.

sentences.zh: 度著《邇英聖覽》十卷、《龜鑒精義》三卷、《編年總錄》八卷，奉詔領諸儒集《武經總要》四十卷。

translations.literal: Du authored ten juan of 《Ertang Sage Perusal》, three of 《Tortoise Mirror Essentials》, eight of 《Chronological General Records》, and received orders leading scholars to compile forty juan of 《Comprehensive Military Essentials》.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote 《Ertang Sage Perusal》 ten juan, 《Tortoise Mirror Essentials》 three, 《Chronological General Records》 eight, and led 《Comprehensive Military Essentials》 forty juan.

sentences.zh: 子諷，集賢校理。

translations.literal: His son Feng was collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Son Feng, Hall of Assembled Worthies collator.

sentences.zh: 張觀，字思正，絳州絳縣人。

translations.literal: Zhang Guan, style name Sizheng, was a man of Jiang County, Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan, styled Sizheng, of Jiang County in Jiang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 少謹願好學，有鄉曲名。

translations.literal: In youth he was cautious and fond of learning, with a name in his district.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful, careful and studious, he was known locally.

sentences.zh: 中服勤辭學科，擢為第一，授將作監丞、通判解州。

translations.literal: He passed the diligent-service literary examination, placed first, and was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Construction Administration and vice commissioner of Jie Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: First in the diligent-service exam, he became Construction vice director and Jie vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會鹽池吏以贓敗，坐失舉劾，降監河中府稅。

translations.literal: When salt-pond clerks were ruined by corruption he was demoted for failure to impeach to supervisor of Hedong prefecture tax.
translations.idiomatic: Salt-pond corruption he failed to impeach and was demoted to Hedong tax supervisor.

sentences.zh: 復通判果州，改秘書省秘書郎。

translations.literal: Restored as Guo Prefecture vice commissioner, changed to Secretary of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Restored Guo vice commissioner, then Palace Library secretary.

sentences.zh: 仁宗即位，遷太常丞，擢右正言、直史館，為三司度支判官，同修起居註，改右司諫、知制誥、判登聞檢院，出知杭州。

translations.literal: When Renzong acceded promoted Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Administration, raised Right Rectifier and straight historian, Three Departments revenue judge, co-compiler of Daily Records, changed Right Secretariat remonstrator, edict drafter, and judge of the Memorial Review Office, sent out as Hangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: At accession he rose through Sacrifices vice director, Right Rectifier, historian, revenue judge, Daily Records co-compiler, remonstrator, drafter, Memorial Review judge, then Hangzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 還判國子監，權發遣開封府事，進為翰林學士、知審官院，累遷左司郎中，以給事中權御史中丞。

translations.literal: On return judged the Directorate of Education, acting director of Kaifeng affairs, advanced Hanlin academician and head of the Court of Appointments, repeatedly promoted Left Secretariat director, as Supervising Censor acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Back he ran Education, acted for Kaifeng, became Hanlin academician and Appointments head, Left Secretariat director, acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 時星流、地震、雷發正月，詔求直言。

translations.literal: At the time meteors fell, the earth quaked, and thunder sounded in the first month; an edict sought blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Meteors, earthquake, and January thunder brought an edict seeking blunt counsel.

sentences.zh: 觀謂：“承平日久，政寬法慢，用度漸侈，風俗漸薄，以致災異。”

translations.literal: Guan said: "Long peace has made government lenient and laws slack, expenditures gradually extravagant and customs gradually thin—thereby producing strange portents."
translations.idiomatic: Guan said long peace had loosened law, raised spending, thinned custom—and brought portents.

sentences.zh: 因上四事：一曰知人，二曰嚴禁，三曰尚質，四曰節用。

translations.literal: He submitted four items: first know men; second strict prohibitions; third value substance; fourth economize.
translations.idiomatic: He urged four things: know men, strict bans, value substance, economize.

sentences.zh: 河北大雨水，又條七事，曰：“導積水以廣播種，緩催欠以省禁錮，寬刑罰以振淹獄，收逃田以募歸復，罷工役以先急務，止配率以阜民財，通商旅以濟艱食。”

translations.literal: Great rain flooded Hebei; he also listed seven items: "Drain standing water to broaden sowing; slow collection of arrears to reduce imprisonment; loosen punishments to revive drowned courts; recover abandoned fields to recruit returnees; halt labor projects for urgent tasks; stop apportionment to enrich people's wealth; open merchants to relieve scarce food."
translations.idiomatic: Hebei floods brought seven remedies: drain fields, slow arrears, loosen punishments, recover fields, halt labor, stop apportionment, open trade.

sentences.zh: 復知審官院，遂拜同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: Restored as head of the Court of Appointments, then appointed Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Restored Appointments head, then Military Affairs vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 康定中，西兵失利，因議點鄉兵，久之不決，遂與王鬷、陳執中俱罷，以資政殿學士、尚書禮部侍郎知相州。

translations.literal: In Kangding when western troops were defeated, because discussion of mustering militia dragged on unresolved, he was dismissed together with Wang Zou and Chen Zhizhong, made Assisting Governance academician and Vice Rites Minister governing Xiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kangding western defeat and stalled militia debate dismissed him with Wang Zou and Chen Zhizhong to Xiang as Assisting Governance academician.

sentences.zh: 徙澶州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Chan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Chan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 河壞孫陳埽及浮梁，州人大恐，或請趨北原以避水患。

translations.literal: The river broke Sun Chen embankment and the floating bridge; the prefecture people were greatly afraid, some asking to flee to the north plain to avoid flood.
translations.idiomatic: The river broke Sun Chen embankment and the bridge; some urged fleeing north.

sentences.zh: 觀曰：“太守獨去，如州民何。”

translations.literal: Guan said: "If the prefect alone leaves, what of the prefecture people?"
translations.idiomatic: Guan said: "If the prefect alone flees, what of the people?"

sentences.zh: 乃躬率卒徒增築之，堤完，水亦退。

translations.literal: He then personally led soldiers to heighten the dike; when the dike was complete the water also receded.
translations.idiomatic: He led soldiers to raise the dike; when finished the water fell.

sentences.zh: 徙鄆州。

translations.literal: Transferred to Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊法，亦東通安邑鹽，而瀕海之地禁私煮。

translations.literal: By old law Yidong also connected Anyi salt, while coastal regions forbade private boiling.
translations.idiomatic: Old law let Yidong use Anyi salt while coasts forbade private boiling.

sentences.zh: 觀上言：“利之所在，百姓趨之，雖日殺於市，恐不能止，請弛禁以便民。”

translations.literal: Guan memorialized: "Where profit lies the people rush, though daily executions in the market I fear it cannot be stopped—please relax the ban to benefit the people."
translations.idiomatic: Guan said profit draws people despite executions—relax the ban for the people.

sentences.zh: 歲免黥配者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Each year those spared tattooing and exile were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yearly tattooing and exile exemptions were countless.

sentences.zh: 歷知應天府、孟州、河南府，以吏部侍郎兼御史中丞。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Yingtian, Meng, and Henan, as Vice Minister of Personnel concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He governed Yingtian, Meng, and Henan, Personnel vice minister and Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 以父居業高年多病，請便郡，以觀文殿學士知許州。

translations.literal: Because his father Juye was aged and often ill he requested a convenient prefecture and was made Observant Culture academician governing Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Father Juye aged and ill, he sought a nearby post and governed Xu as Observant Culture academician.

sentences.zh: 月餘，拜左丞。

translations.literal: After a month and more appointed Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，哀毀過人，既練而卒。

translations.literal: Mourning his father he grieved beyond others and died after the second-year mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Father mourning grieved him past measure; he died after second-year mourning.

sentences.zh: 贈吏部尚書，謚文孝。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Minister of Personnel, posthumous title Wenxiao.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Personnel Minister, posthumous Wenxiao.

sentences.zh: 觀性至孝，初為秘書郎，其父方為州從事，因上書願以官授父。

translations.literal: Guan's nature was utmost filial; when first a secretary his father was still a prefecture staff officer; he memorialized wishing to grant his office to his father.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply filial, as secretary he asked to give his post to his father, then a prefecture aide.

sentences.zh: 真宗嘉之，以居業為京官。

translations.literal: Zhenzong approved and made Juye a capital official.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzong made Juye a capital official.

sentences.zh: 及觀貴，居業繇恩至太府卿。

translations.literal: When Guan rose high, Juye through favor reached Vice Director of the Imperial Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan rose, Juye through favor became Treasury vice director.

sentences.zh: 居業嘗過洛，嘉其山川風物，曰：“吾得老於此足矣。”

translations.literal: Juye once passed Luoyang, praised its mountains, rivers, and scenery, and said: "I could grow old here and be satisfied."
translations.idiomatic: Juye passing Luoyang praised its scenery: "I could grow old here content."

sentences.zh: 觀於是買田宅、營林榭，以適其意。

translations.literal: Guan thereupon bought fields, houses, and forest pavilions to suit his wish.
translations.idiomatic: Guan bought fields, houses, and pavilions for him.

sentences.zh: 早起奉藥、膳，然後出視事，未嘗一日廢也。

translations.literal: Rising early to present medicine and meals, then going out to handle affairs—never a day neglected.
translations.idiomatic: He rose early for medicine and meals before office—never a day missed.

sentences.zh: 趣尚恬曠，持廉少欲，平生書必為楷字，無一行草，類其為人。

translations.literal: His bent was tranquil breadth; he held integrity with few desires; all his life in writing he used regular script, never a line of cursive—like his person.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil and frugal, he wrote only regular script, never cursive—like his character.

sentences.zh: 仁宗飛白書“清”字賜觀，以賞其節。

translations.literal: Renzong's flying-white script character "Qing" was granted Guan to reward his integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong's flying-white "Qing" rewarded his integrity.

sentences.zh: 然於吏事非所長，知開封府，民犯夜禁，觀詰之曰：“有人見否？”

translations.literal: Yet he was not skilled in clerical matters; governing Kaifeng, when a man violated the night curfew Guan questioned him: "Was there someone who saw?"
translations.idiomatic: Weak in clerical work, at Kaifeng he asked a curfew violator: "Was anyone watching?"

sentences.zh: 眾傳以為笑。

translations.literal: The crowd spread it as a joke.
translations.idiomatic: People laughed.

sentences.zh: 鄭戩，字天休，蘇州吳縣人。

translations.literal: Zheng Jian, style name Tianxiu, was a man of Wu County, Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Jian, styled Tianxiu, of Wu County, Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 早孤力學。

translations.literal: Orphaned early, he studied with force.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, he studied hard.

sentences.zh: 客京師，事楊億，以屬辭知名，後復還吳。

translations.literal: As a guest in the capital he served Yang Yi and was known for literary composition; later he returned to Wu.
translations.idiomatic: In the capital he studied under Yang Yi and was known for prose; later he returned to Wu.

sentences.zh: 及億卒，賓客弟子散去，戩乃倍道會葬。

translations.literal: When Yi died, guests and disciples dispersed; Jian traveled day and night to attend the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: When Yi died Jian rushed day and night to the funeral while others dispersed.

sentences.zh: 舉進士，擢甲科，授太常寺奉禮郎、簽書寧國軍節度判官事，召試學士院，為光祿寺丞、集賢校理、通判越州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, placed in the top grade, appointed Court Gentleman for Offering of the Imperial Sacrifices Administration and secretary of Ningguo Army military commissioner, summoned to the Hanlin examination, made Vice Director of the Imperial Household Administration, Hall collator, and Yue Prefecture vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Top-grade jinshi, Sacrifices Court Gentleman and Ningguo secretary, Hanlin exam, Household vice director, Hall collator, Yue vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 還，改太子中允、同知太常禮院，註釋御制《發願文》、《三寶贊》，升直史館、三司戶部判官，同修起居注，以右正言知制誥。

translations.literal: On return changed to Central Drafting Attendant of the Heir Apparent and concurrent director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices; annotated the imperial 《Vow Text》 and 《Three Treasures Praise》; promoted straight historian of the Historiography Office and Revenue-section judge of the Three Departments, co-compiler of Daily Records, as Right Rectifier and edict drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Back he became Heir Apparent Central Drafting Attendant, Sacrifices director, annotated imperial 《Vow Text》 and 《Three Treasures Praise》, historian, revenue judge, Daily Records co-compiler, Right Rectifier and drafter.

sentences.zh: 判國子監；

translations.literal: Judged the Directorate of Education;
translations.idiomatic: Judged the Directorate of Education;

sentences.zh: 選明經生講解經義。

translations.literal: selected students who had passed the classics examination to lecture on canonical meaning.
translations.idiomatic: selected classics-exam graduates to lecture on scripture.

sentences.zh: 徙知審刑院，遷起居舍人、龍圖閣直學士、權知開封府。

translations.literal: Transferred to head the Court of Judicial Review, promoted Drafting Gentleman, Dragon Hall straight academician, and acting prefect of Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Judicial Review head, Drafting Gentleman, Dragon Hall straight academician, acting Kaifeng prefect.

sentences.zh: 吏馮士為奸利，有告士元受賕藏禁書者，戩窮治之。

translations.literal: Clerk Feng Shi sought illicit profit; someone reported Feng Shiyuan took bribes and hid banned books; Jian exhaustively tried the case.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk Feng Shi profiteered; reports said Feng Shiyuan took bribes and hid banned books—Jian tried it thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 辭連宰相呂夷簡、知樞密院盛度、參知政事程琳，遂逮捕夷簡子公綽、公弼參劾其狀。

translations.literal: The case implicated chief minister Lü Yijian, Military Affairs head Sheng Du, and Vice Participant Cheng Lin; he then arrested Yijian's sons Gongchuo and Gongbi and impeached their conduct.
translations.idiomatic: It implicated Lü Yijian, Sheng Du, and Cheng Lin; Jian arrested Yijian's sons and impeached them.

sentences.zh: 既而士元流海島，度、琳坐嘗交關士元罷去，其餘絀罰者，自御史中丞孔道輔、天章閣待制龐籍又十餘人，朝議畏其皦核。

translations.literal: Thereafter Shiyuan was exiled to a sea island; Du and Lin were dismissed for once associating with Shiyuan; the rest demoted or fined—from Vice Censor-in-Chief Kong Daofu and Tianzhang Hall awaiting-formatter Pang Ji more than ten—court opinion feared his severity.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan was exiled; Du and Lin fell for Shiyuan ties; a dozen officials including Kong Daofu and Pang Ji were punished—court feared Jian's severity.

sentences.zh: 戩敏強善聽決，喜出不意，獨假貸細民，即豪宗大姓，繩治益急，政有能跡。

translations.literal: Jian was keen and forceful, skilled at hearing and deciding, delighted in the unexpected; he alone indulged common folk, but toward great clans and powerful surnames he bound law ever tighter—his governance showed ability.
translations.idiomatic: Keen and decisive, Jian surprised opponents, indulged commoners, and tightened law on great clans—effective rule.

sentences.zh: 徙權三司使，復轉運使考課格，分別殿最。

translations.literal: Transferred acting Three Departments commissioner; restored transport commissioner evaluation forms, distinguishing highest and lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Made acting Three Departments commissioner; restored transport evaluations with highest and lowest ranks.

sentences.zh: 又勾較三司出入，得羨錢四百萬緡，以右諫議大夫、同知樞密院改樞密副使。

translations.literal: Again audited Three Departments receipts and disbursements, finding four million strings surplus; as Right Remonstrance Censor and concurrent Military Affairs commissioner changed to Military Affairs vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Auditing Three Departments funds found four million strings surplus; Right Remonstrance Censor became Military Affairs vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 戩與參知政事宋庠，為宰相呂夷簡所忌，與庠皆罷，以資政殿學士知杭州。

translations.literal: Jian and Vice Participant Song Xiu were disliked by chief minister Lü Yijian; both were dismissed and Jian made Assisting Governance academician governing Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Yijian disliked Jian and Song Xiu; both were dismissed; Jian governed Hangzhou as Assisting Governance academician.

sentences.zh: 錢塘湖溉民田數十頃，錢氏置撩清軍，以疏淤填之患。

translations.literal: Qiantang Lake irrigated tens of thousands of mu; the Qian house established a dredging-clearing army to relieve silting.
translations.idiomatic: Qiantang Lake irrigated tens of thousands of mu; the Qian house kept a dredging corps against silting.

sentences.zh: 既納國後不復治，葑土堙塞，為豪族僧坊所占冒，湖水益狹。

translations.literal: After entering the realm it was no longer maintained; duckweed soil blocked it and powerful clans and monasteries encroached—the lake grew ever narrower.
translations.idiomatic: After annexation it was neglected; silt and encroachment by clans and monasteries shrank the lake.

sentences.zh: 戩發屬縣丁夫數萬辟之，民賴其利。

translations.literal: Jian mobilized tens of thousands of corvée laborers from subordinate counties to open it; the people relied on the benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Jian mobilized tens of thousands of county laborers to dredge it; people benefited.

sentences.zh: 事聞，詔本郡歲治如戩法。

translations.literal: The matter was reported; an edict ordered the prefecture yearly to maintain it by Jian's method.
translations.idiomatic: Reported up, the court ordered yearly maintenance by Jian's method.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，徙并州，道改鄆州，又徙永興軍。

translations.literal: Promoted Supervising Censor, moved to Bing Prefecture, on the road changed to Yan Prefecture, again moved to Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Supervising Censor, sent to Bing, diverted to Yan, then Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 建言：“凡軍行所須，願下有司相緩急，析為三等，非急罷去。”

translations.literal: He memorialized: "All army march needs should be sent to offices to weigh urgency, divided into three grades, and what is not urgent abolished."
translations.idiomatic: He urged ranking army needs in three grades of urgency and abolishing non-urgent items.

sentences.zh: 先是，衙吏輸木京師，浮渭泛河，多漂沒，既至，則斥不中程，往往破家不能償，戩奏歲減二十餘萬；

translations.literal: Previously yamen clerks shipped timber to the capital, floating on the Wei and Yellow rivers—many sank; when arrived they were rejected as not meeting measure, often ruining families unable to pay; Jian memorialized reducing more than two hundred thousand yearly;
translations.idiomatic: Clerks shipping timber to the capital lost much on the rivers and faced ruin when timber failed measure—Jian cut over two hundred thousand strings yearly;

sentences.zh: 又奏罷括糴，以勸民積粟。

translations.literal: he also memorialized abolishing forced grain purchase to encourage the people to store grain.
translations.idiomatic: he also ended forced grain purchase to encourage storage.

sentences.zh: 長安故都多豪惡，戩治之尚嚴，甚者至黥竄，人皆惕息。

translations.literal: Chang'an as an old capital had many fierce and wicked; Jian governed with severity still, the worst tattooed and exiled—all were wary.
translations.idiomatic: Old-capital Chang'an had fierce magnates; Jian ruled harshly, tattooing and exiling the worst—people feared him.

sentences.zh: 未幾，為陜西四路都總管兼經略、安撫、招討使，駐涇州，聽便宜從事。

translations.literal: Before long made overall commander of the four Shaanxi circuits with pacification, comfort, and punitive powers, stationed at Jing Prefecture, hearing matters as expedient required.
translations.idiomatic: Soon overall commander of four Shaanxi circuits with full frontier powers, based at Jing.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Promoted Vice Rites Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Vice Rites Minister.

sentences.zh: 時知慶州滕宗諒、知渭州張亢過用公使錢，戩致於法。

translations.literal: At the time Qing Prefecture prefect Teng Zongliang and Wei Prefecture prefect Zhang Kang overused public-service funds; Jian brought them to law.
translations.idiomatic: Qing prefect Teng Zongliang and Wei prefect Zhang Kang misused public funds; Jian prosecuted them.

sentences.zh: 行邊至鎮戎軍，趣蓮花堡，天寒，與將佐置酒，元昊擁兵近塞。

translations.literal: Patrolling the border to Zhenrong Army he hastened to Lotus Fort; the weather was cold and he set wine with generals; Yuan Hao massed troops near the border.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenrong in cold weather he drank with generals at Lotus Fort while Yuan Hao neared the border.

sentences.zh: 會暮塵起，有報敵騎至者，戩曰：“此必三川將按邊回，非敵騎也。”

translations.literal: At dusk dust rose; there was report enemy cavalry had come; Jian said: "This must be the San River general returning from patrolling the border—not enemy cavalry."
translations.idiomatic: Dusk dust brought an alarm; Jian said it was a San River patrol returning, not enemies.

sentences.zh: 已而果然。

translations.literal: It was indeed so.
translations.idiomatic: It was.

sentences.zh: 及疆事少寧，詔還，知永興軍。

translations.literal: When frontier affairs grew somewhat calm an edict recalled him; he governed Yongxing Army.
translations.idiomatic: When the frontier calmed he was recalled to govern Yongxing Army.

sentences.zh: 初，靜邊砦主劉滬謀築水洛、結公二城，以通秦、渭援兵，招生羌大王族為邊衛。

translations.literal: Earlier Jingbian Fort commander Liu Hu planned to build Shuilo and Jiegong cities to link Qin and Wei relief troops and recruit great Qiang clans as border guards.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Liu Hu at Jingbian Fort planned Shuilo and Jiegong cities to link Qin-Wei relief and recruit Qiang clans.

sentences.zh: 戩使滬與著作佐郎董士廉督其役。

translations.literal: Jian ordered Hu with Editorial Assistant Dong Shilian to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: Jian put Hu and Editorial Assistant Dong Shilian in charge.

sentences.zh: 會罷戩四路，宣撫使韓琦、知渭州尹洙皆以為不便，召滬、士廉罷役歸，不聽。

translations.literal: When Jian's four-circuit post ended, Pacification Commissioner Han Qi and Wei prefect Yin Zhu all thought it unwise and summoned Hu and Shilian to halt work and return—they would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: When Jian left the frontier Han Qi and Yin Zhu halted the works; Hu and Shilian refused.

sentences.zh: 乃使裨將狄青將兵以往，械送德順軍獄。

translations.literal: He then sent subordinate general Di Qing with troops; they were shackled and sent to Deshun Army prison.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Di Qing, who shackled them for Deshun prison.

sentences.zh: 戩力爭於朝，卒城之。

translations.literal: Jian argued forcefully at court and in the end the cities were built.
translations.idiomatic: Jian fought at court and the cities were finished.

sentences.zh: 進戶部侍郎、資政殿大學士、知并州。

translations.literal: Promoted Revenue Section director, Grand Assisting Governance academician, and Bing Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Revenue director, Grand Assisting Governance academician, Bing prefect.

sentences.zh: 契丹與元昊方交兵，邊奏互上，獨戩不以聞。

translations.literal: Khitan and Yuan Hao were fighting; border reports came in alternately—only Jian did not report.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan and Yuan Hao fought; border reports alternated—only Jian stayed silent.

sentences.zh: 詔遣使問其故，戩對曰：“敵自相攻，中國不足憂也。”

translations.literal: An edict sent envoys to ask the reason; Jian replied: "Enemies attacking each other—the Middle Kingdom need not worry."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, Jian said enemies fighting each other were no worry for China.

sentences.zh: 麟、府間有棄地曰草城川，戩募土人為弓箭手，計口給田。

translations.literal: Between Lin and Fu there was abandoned land called Grass City Stream; Jian recruited natives as archers, allotting fields by mouth.
translations.idiomatic: At Grass City Stream between Lin and Fu he recruited native archers with land by household.

sentences.zh: 初，兵興，用不足。

translations.literal: At first when war began funds were insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: War had left funds short.

sentences.zh: 河東行鐵錢，山多炭、鐵，鼓鑄利厚，重辟不能止。

translations.literal: Hedong used iron coin; mountains had much coal and iron—casting profit was thick and heavy penalties could not stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong used iron coin; rich coal and iron made casting profitable despite harsh law.

sentences.zh: 戩乃請三當一。

translations.literal: Jian then requested three-for-one exchange.
translations.idiomatic: Jian ordered three old coins for one new.

sentences.zh: 令既下，兵民相扇動，數千人邀走馬承受訴。

translations.literal: When the order descended soldiers and civilians stirred each other; several thousand people intercepted the traveling memorial receiver to complain.
translations.idiomatic: The order stirred thousands who blocked the memorial receiver to protest.

sentences.zh: 承受，中貴人，不能遏。

translations.literal: The receiver was a palace eunuch and could not restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch receiver could not restrain them.

sentences.zh: 又群噪州門，守門者拒不得入。

translations.literal: They also clamored at the prefecture gate; gatekeepers refused entry.
translations.idiomatic: They mobbed the prefecture gate and were kept out.

sentences.zh: 戩聞，悉召至庭下，推首謀者數十人，黥隸他州，事乃定。

translations.literal: Jian heard, summoned all to the courtyard, pushed out several dozen ringleaders, tattooed and assigned them to other prefectures—the affair was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Jian summoned them, tattooed dozens of ringleaders and sent them elsewhere—the riot ended.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，改宣徽北院使，拜奉國軍節度使，卒。

translations.literal: Promoted Personnel vice minister, changed Northern Hall of the Imperial Entertainment envoy, appointed Fengguo Army military commissioner, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Personnel vice minister, Entertainment envoy, Fengguo military commissioner, then died.

sentences.zh: 贈太尉，謚文肅。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Marshal, posthumous title Wensu.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Grand Marshal, posthumous Wensu.

sentences.zh: 戩遇事，果敢必行。

translations.literal: In affairs Jian was bold and sure to act.
translations.idiomatic: Jian acted boldly and decisively.

sentences.zh: 然憑氣近俠，用刑峻深，士民多怨之。

translations.literal: Yet relying on spirit he neared knight-errantry; punishments were harsh and deep—gentlemen and commoners mostly resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he was chivalrous and harsh—officials and people resented him.

sentences.zh: 明鎬，字化基，密州安丘人。

translations.literal: Ming Gao, style name Huaji, was a man of Anqiu, Mi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Gao, styled Huaji, of Anqiu in Mi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 中進士第，補蘄州防禦推官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed defense push officer of Qi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jinshi, then Qi defense push officer.

sentences.zh: 真宗崩，上《真頌》四十六篇，改大理寺丞。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong died he submitted forty-six chapters of 《True Eulogies》 and was changed to reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: At Zhenzong's death he submitted forty-six 《True Eulogies》 and became Judicial Review reviewer.

sentences.zh: 薛奎領秦州，辟為節度判官。

translations.literal: Xue Kui led Qin Prefecture and recruited him as military commissioner secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Kui took Qin and made him military secretary.

sentences.zh: 奎徙益州，辟知錄事參軍。

translations.literal: Kui moved to Yi Prefecture and recruited him as registrar.
translations.idiomatic: Kui moved to Yi and made him registrar.

sentences.zh: 程琳代奎，奏為簽書節度判官，就通判州事，遷太常博士。

translations.literal: Cheng Lin replaced Kui and memorialized him as signed military commissioner secretary, then vice prefect on the spot, promoted Erudite of the Imperial Sacrifices Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng Lin made him signed military secretary and acting vice prefect, then Sacrifices erudite.

sentences.zh: 還朝，仁宗問鎬所能，奎稱其沈鷙有謀，能斷大事，除開封推官。

translations.literal: On return to court Renzong asked what Gao could do; Kui said he was deep and fierce with strategy, able to decide great affairs—appointed Kaifeng investigating officer.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong asked Kui, who called Gao deep, fierce, and decisive—Kaifeng investigating officer.

sentences.zh: 獻《六冗書》，進尚書祠部員外郎，為三司戶部判官，改刑部員外郎、京東轉運使，遷兵部員外郎、直史館、益州路轉運使。

translations.literal: He submitted 《Six Redundancies》 and was promoted Vice Director of the Rites Section, Three Departments revenue judge, War Section vice director, straight historian, and Yi Circuit transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted 《Six Redundancies》, rose through Rites, revenue judge, War vice director, historian, Yi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，民無積聚，盜賊間發，鎬為平物價，募民為兵，人賴以安。

translations.literal: When famine struck the people had no stores and bandits arose intermittently; Gao stabilized prices and recruited men as soldiers—the people relied on safety.
translations.idiomatic: In famine he stabilized prices and recruited militia—people were safe.

sentences.zh: 知陵州，楚應幾贓敗，或告以先期奏之，鎬曰：“獲罪則已，安可欺朝廷耶？”

translations.literal: Governing Ling Prefecture, Chu Yingji's corruption was exposed; some said Gao had reported early; Gao said: "If guilty so be it—how could I deceive the court?"
translations.idiomatic: At Ling, Chu Yingji fell; told he had reported early, Gao said guilt was enough—he would not deceive the court.

sentences.zh: 卒坐失察，降知同州。

translations.literal: In the end he was punished for failure to inspect and demoted to Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Tong for failure to inspect.

sentences.zh: 未逾月，會元昊寇延州，起為陜西轉運使。

translations.literal: Within a month Yuan Hao raided Yan Prefecture; he was raised as Shaanxi transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: A month later Yuan Hao raided Yan; Gao became Shaanxi transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 虜破金明砦，既去，議修復其城，帥臣擁兵不即進，而鎬止以百餘騎，自督將士，一月而成。

translations.literal: The barbarians broke Jinming Fort and left; debate restored the fort while commanders held troops and did not advance—Gao with only a hundred-odd horsemen personally supervised officers and finished in a month.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinming Fort fell, commanders stalled; Gao rebuilt it in a month with a hundred horsemen.

sentences.zh: 又嘗閱同州廂軍，得材武者三百餘人，教以強弩，奏為清邊軍，號最驍悍。

translations.literal: He also once reviewed Tong garrison troops, found more than three hundred skilled and martial, taught them powerful crossbows, memorialized them as Clear Border Army—the name for most fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing Tong garrison he trained three hundred crossbowmen as Clear Border Army—fiercest troops.

sentences.zh: 其後，陜西、河東頗仿置之。

translations.literal: Later Shaanxi and Hedong largely imitated this.
translations.idiomatic: Later Shaanxi and Hedong copied the model.

sentences.zh: 遷戶部郎中、直昭文館、知陜州，徙江、淮制置發運使。

translations.literal: Promoted Revenue Section director, straight Zhaowen Hall academician, and Shaanxi prefect; moved Jiang-Huai provisioning transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Revenue director, Zhaowen straight academician, Shaanxi prefect; slated for Jiang-Huai transport.

sentences.zh: 未行，會賊破豐州，擢天章閣待制、河東都轉運使。

translations.literal: Before departing, when bandits broke Feng Prefecture he was raised Tianzhang Hall awaiting-formatter and Hedong overall transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before leaving, Feng fell to bandits; he became Tianzhang awaiting-formatter and Hedong transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 修建寧中候百勝砦、鎮川清塞堡，凡五城，以勞遷左司郎中。

translations.literal: He built Jianning Zhonghou Hundred Victories Fort, Zhenchuan Clear Barrier Fort—five cities in all—for merit promoted Left Secretariat director.
translations.idiomatic: He built five frontier forts including Jianning and Zhenchuan and was promoted Left Secretariat director.

sentences.zh: 明年，擢龍圖閣直學士、知并州。

translations.literal: The next year promoted Dragon Hall straight academician and Bing Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Next year Dragon Hall straight academician and Bing prefect.

sentences.zh: 鎬大巡邊以備賊。

translations.literal: Gao made a great border tour to guard against bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Gao toured the border heavily against bandits.

sentences.zh: 時邊任多紈袴子弟，鎬乃取尤不職者杖之，疲軟者皆自解去，遂奏擇習事者守堡砦。

translations.literal: At the time many frontier posts had silk-robed sons; Gao took the most incompetent and flogged them—the weak all resigned, then he memorialized selecting experienced men to hold forts.
translations.idiomatic: He flogged incompetent frontier sons until they quit, then staffed forts with experienced men.

sentences.zh: 軍行，娼婦多從之，鎬欲驅逐，惡傷士卒心，會有忿爭殺娼婦者，吏執以白，鎬曰：“彼來軍中何耶？”

translations.literal: On march many camp followers went along; Gao wished to drive them off but feared hurting troop morale—then someone in anger killed a camp follower; the officer arrested him and reported; Gao said: "What business had they coming to the army?"
translations.idiomatic: Camp followers marched with the army; when one was killed Gao asked what business they had in camp.

sentences.zh: 縱去不治，娼婦聞皆散走。

translations.literal: He released them without punishment; hearing this camp followers all scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He released the killer; camp followers fled.

sentences.zh: 以樞密直學士、左諫議大夫知成德軍，入知開封府。

translations.literal: As Military Affairs straight academician and Left Remonstrance Censor he governed Chengde Army; entered to govern Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Military Affairs straight academician and Left Remonstrance Censor at Chengde; then Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 王則叛，命鎬為體量安撫使；

translations.literal: Wang Ze rebelled; Gao was appointed measurement-and-comfort commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ze rebelled; Gao was measurement-and-comfort commissioner;

sentences.zh: 則未下，又命參知政事文彥博為宣撫使，以鎬副之。

translations.literal: before Ze fell, Vice Participant Wen Yanbo was also appointed pacification commissioner with Gao as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: before Ze fell Wen Yanbo was pacification commissioner with Gao deputy.

sentences.zh: 貝州平，遷端明殿學士、給事中、權三司使，諸將悉超遷，都虞候、士卒八千四百人，第其功為五等，每等遷一資。

translations.literal: When Bei Prefecture was pacified he was promoted Illustrious Hall academician, Supervising Censor, acting Three Departments commissioner; all generals were promoted beyond rank—eight thousand four hundred commanders and soldiers ranked in five grades, each grade one promotion.
translations.idiomatic: Bei pacified, he became Illustrious Hall academician, Supervising Censor, acting Three Departments commissioner; eight thousand four hundred men ranked five grades for promotion.

sentences.zh: 彥博數推鎬功，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Yanbo repeatedly pushed Gao's merit; he was appointed Vice Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo praised Gao; he became Vice Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 已而疽發背，帝謂輔臣曰：“鎬忠亮有勞，及其未亂，思一見之。”

translations.literal: Soon carbuncle broke on his back; the emperor told chief ministers: "Gao is loyal and bright with merit; before it worsens I wish once to see him."
translations.idiomatic: A back carbuncle opened; the emperor told ministers he wished to see loyal Gao before it worsened.

sentences.zh: 臨問，惻然曰：“方賴卿謀國事，何遽被疾！”

translations.literal: On visiting him he said with compassion: "I rely on you to plan state affairs—why suddenly stricken!"
translations.idiomatic: Visiting, he said he relied on Gao for state affairs—why so ill!

sentences.zh: 鎬氣憊，猶能頓首謝。

translations.literal: Gao was exhausted in breath yet could still bow in thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Exhausted, Gao still bowed thanks.

sentences.zh: 翌日，卒，謚文烈。

translations.literal: The next day he died; posthumous title Wenlie.
translations.idiomatic: He died next day; posthumous Wenlie.

sentences.zh: 鎬端挺寡言，所至安靜有體，而遇事不茍，為世所推重。

translations.literal: Gao was upright and sparing of words; wherever he went he was quiet and measured, yet in affairs not lax—esteemed by the age.
translations.idiomatic: Upright and taciturn, calm and measured, yet firm in affairs—widely esteemed.

translations.literal: 〈Appendix〉
translations.idiomatic: 〈Appendix〉

sentences.zh: 王則

translations.literal: Wang Ze
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ze

sentences.zh: 王則者，本涿州人。

translations.literal: Wang Ze was originally a man of Zhuo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ze was from Zhuo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歲饑，流至恩州，自賣為人牧羊，後隸宣毅軍為小校。

translations.literal: In famine years he drifted to En Prefecture, sold himself to herd sheep, later entered the Xuanyi Army as a junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: Famine sent him to En; he sold himself as a shepherd, then joined the Xuanyi Army as a junior officer.

sentences.zh: 恩、冀俗妖幻，相與習《五龍》、《滴淚》等經及圖讖諸書，言釋迦佛衰謝，彌勒佛當持世。

translations.literal: En and Ji customs favored demonic illusions; they together studied scriptures such as 《Five Dragons》 and 《Dripping Tears》 and prognostication books, saying Shakyamuni Buddha's age was declining and Maitreya Buddha would hold the world.
translations.idiomatic: En and Ji favored occult sects studying 《Five Dragons》, 《Dripping Tears》, and omens that Maitreya would succeed the fading Buddha.

sentences.zh: 初，則去涿，母與之訣別，刺“福”字於其背以為記。

translations.literal: When Ze first left Zhuo his mother parted from him and pricked the character "Fortune" on his back as a mark.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving Zhuo his mother tattooed "Fortune" on his back.

sentences.zh: 妖人因妄傳字隱起，爭信事之，而州吏張巒、卜吉主其謀，黨連德、齊諸州，約以慶歷八年正旦，斷澶州浮梁，亂河北。

translations.literal: Sectarians from false transmission said the character hid and rose; they vied to believe and serve him; prefecture clerks Zhang Luan and Bu Ji led the plot, linking De and Qi prefectures, agreeing on Qingli year eight first month to cut the Chan floating bridge and disorder Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Sectarians said the tattooed character would rise; clerks Zhang Luan and Bu Ji plotted with De and Qi to cut the Chan bridge in Qingli year eight and disorder Hebei.

sentences.zh: 會其黨潘方凈以書謁北京留守賈昌朝，事覺被執，故不待期，亟以七年冬至叛。

translations.literal: Their clique Pan Fangjing presented a letter to Beijing resident commissioner Jia Changchao; the affair was exposed and he was arrested—therefore not waiting for the date they urgently rebelled on the seventh year winter solstice.
translations.idiomatic: Clique member Pan Fangjing exposed the plot to Jia Changchao; they rebelled early on the seventh-year winter solstice.

sentences.zh: 時知州張得一方與官謁天慶觀，則率其徒劫庫兵，得一走保驍捷營。

translations.literal: At the time prefect Zhang Deyi was with officials paying respects at Tianqing Temple; Ze led his band to seize armory weapons; Deyi fled to the Valiant Cavalry camp.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zhang Deyi was at Tianqing Temple; Ze seized the armory while Deyi fled to Valiant Cavalry camp.

sentences.zh: 賊焚門，執得一囚之。

translations.literal: The bandits burned the gate and seized Deyi, imprisoning him.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits burned the gate and imprisoned Deyi.

sentences.zh: 兵馬都監、內殿承制田斌以從卒巷鬥，不勝而出。

translations.literal: Horse-and-arms director and Inner Hall commissioner Tian Bin fought in alleys with followers and could not overcome them and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Director Tian Bin fought in alleys and fled defeated.

sentences.zh: 城扉闔，提點刑獄田京、任黃裳持印，棄其家縋城出，保南關。

translations.literal: City gates closed; criminal law intendant Tian Jing and Ren Huangshang took seals, abandoned their families, lowered themselves from the wall, and fled to South Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Gates closed; Tian Jing and Ren Huangshang fled by rope to South Pass.

sentences.zh: 賊從通判董元亨取軍資庫鑰，元亨拒之，殺元亨。

translations.literal: The bandits followed Vice Prefect Dong Yuanheng to take the military stores key; Yuanheng refused and they killed Yuanheng.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits demanded the stores key from Dong Yuanheng; he refused and was killed.

sentences.zh: 又出獄囚，囚有憾司理參軍王獎者，遂殺獎。

translations.literal: They also released prisoners; a prisoner bore a grudge against judicial assistant Wang Jiang and killed Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: They freed prisoners; one killed judicial assistant Wang Jiang.

sentences.zh: 既而節度判官李浩、清河令齊開、主簿王湙皆被害。

translations.literal: Then military commissioner judge Li Hao, Qinghe magistrate Qi Kai, and registrar Wang Ying were all harmed.
translations.idiomatic: Judge Li Hao, magistrate Qi Kai, and registrar Wang Ying were killed.

sentences.zh: 則僣號東平郡王，以張巒為宰相，卜吉為樞密使，建國曰安陽。

translations.literal: Ze falsely styled himself Prince of Dongping, made Zhang Luan chief minister and Bu Ji Military Affairs commissioner, and founded the state Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Ze styled himself Prince of Dongping, made Zhang Luan chief minister and Bu Ji Military Affairs head, and founded Anyang.

sentences.zh: 榜所居門曰中京，居室廄庫皆立名號，改年曰得聖，以十二月為正月。

translations.literal: He posted on his dwelling gate "Central Capital," naming dwellings, stables, and stores, changed the era to Desheng, and made the twelfth month the first month.
translations.idiomatic: He called his gate Central Capital, named quarters and stores, era Desheng, twelfth month first month.

sentences.zh: 百姓年十二以上、七十以下，皆涅其面曰“義軍破趙得勝”。

translations.literal: Commoners twelve and above and seventy below were all tattooed on the face "Righteous Army breaks Zhao and wins."
translations.idiomatic: Subjects twelve to seventy were face-tattooed "Righteous Army breaks Zhao and wins."

sentences.zh: 旗幟號令，率以“佛”為稱。

translations.literal: Banners, flags, and orders mostly used "Buddha" as title.
translations.idiomatic: Flags and orders mostly used "Buddha."

sentences.zh: 城以一樓為一州，書州名，補其徒為知州，每面置一總管。

translations.literal: The city made each tower a prefecture, wrote prefecture names, appointed followers as prefects, and set one overall commander on each face.
translations.idiomatic: Each tower became a prefecture with named commanders and follower-prefects.

sentences.zh: 然縋城下者日眾。

translations.literal: Yet those who lowered themselves from the wall daily grew numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Daily more men lowered from the wall.

sentences.zh: 於是令守者伍伍為保，一人縋，餘悉斬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered defenders grouped in fives as mutual surety—if one lowered, the rest were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Defenders were grouped in fives: one descender meant all five were beheaded.

sentences.zh: 有州民汪文慶、郭斌、趙宗本、汪順者，自城上系書射鎬帳，約為內應，夜垂縆以引官軍。

translations.literal: Prefecture men Wang Wenqing, Guo Bin, Zhao Zongben, and Wang Shun from atop the wall tied letters and shot them into Gao's tent, agreeing as inside agents to lower ropes at night to draw in government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenqing, Guo Bin, Zhao Zongben, and Wang Shun shot letters into Gao's camp promising night ropes for government troops.

sentences.zh: 既內數百人，焚樓櫓，賊覺，率眾拒戰。

translations.literal: After several hundred were inside they burned towers; the bandits noticed and led the crowd to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds entered and burned towers; bandits fought back.

sentences.zh: 初，官軍既登，欲專其功，斷縆以絕後來者。

translations.literal: At first when government troops had ascended they wished to monopolize merit and cut the ropes to cut off those coming after.
translations.idiomatic: Troops inside cut the ropes to monopolize credit and block reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 及與賊戰，兵寡不敵，與文慶等復縋而下。

translations.literal: When fighting the bandits, troops were few and could not match; with Wenqing and the rest they lowered themselves again.
translations.idiomatic: Outnumbered, they lowered themselves again with the agents.

sentences.zh: 是夜，城幾克。

translations.literal: That night the city was nearly taken.
translations.idiomatic: That night the city nearly fell.

sentences.zh: 則期正月十四日出要劫契丹使，諜者以告。

translations.literal: Ze planned on the fourteenth of the first month to go out and intercept the Khitan envoy; spies reported.
translations.idiomatic: Ze planned to ambush the Khitan envoy on the fourteenth; spies told Gao.

sentences.zh: 鎬遣殿侍安素伏兵西門，賊果以數百人夜出，伏發，皆就獲。

translations.literal: Gao sent palace attendant An Su to ambush at the west gate; the bandits indeed sent several hundred out at night; the ambush sprang and all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Gao ambushed the west gate; hundreds of bandits were captured.

sentences.zh: 城峻不可攻，乃為距闉，將成，為賊所焚。

translations.literal: The walls were high and could not be assaulted; they therefore built siege screens; when nearly complete the bandits burned them.
translations.idiomatic: Walls were too high to storm; siege screens were burned by bandits.

sentences.zh: 遂即南城為地道，日攻其北牽制之。

translations.literal: They then tunneled from the south wall, daily attacking the north to pin them.
translations.idiomatic: They tunneled from the south while attacking the north daily.

sentences.zh: 及文彥博至，穴通城中，選壯士中夜由地道入，眾登城。

translations.literal: When Wen Yanbo arrived the tunnel reached inside the city; strong men were chosen to enter at midnight through the tunnel and the crowd ascended the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo arrived; troops entered by tunnel at midnight and took the wall.

sentences.zh: 賊縱火牛，官軍以槍中牛鼻，牛還攻之，賊大潰，開東門遁。

translations.literal: The bandits drove fire oxen; government troops shot the oxen's noses with spears and the oxen turned to attack; the bandits broke greatly, opened the east gate, and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Fire oxen were turned back with spears; bandits fled east.

sentences.zh: 閣門祗候張姻緣壕與戰，死之。

translations.literal: Gate attendant Zhang Yin fought along the moat and died.
translations.idiomatic: Gate attendant Zhang Yin died fighting at the moat.

sentences.zh: 總管王信捕得則，其餘眾保村舍，皆焚死。

translations.literal: Overall commander Wang Xin captured Ze; the rest held village houses and were all burned to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xin captured Ze; holdouts in villages were burned.

sentences.zh: 檻送則京師，支解以徇。

translations.literal: Ze was caged and sent to the capital and dismembered to display.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was sent to the capital and dismembered as a warning.

sentences.zh: 則叛凡六十六日。

translations.literal: Ze's rebellion lasted altogether sixty-six days.
translations.idiomatic: The rebellion lasted sixty-six days.

sentences.zh: 王堯臣

translations.literal: Wang Yaochen
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yaochen

sentences.zh: 王堯臣，字伯庸，應天府虞城人。

translations.literal: Wang Yaochen, style name Boyong, was a man of Yucheng, Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yaochen, styled Boyong, of Yucheng in Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舉進士第一，授將作監丞、通判湖州。

translations.literal: He placed first in the jinshi examination and was appointed Vice Director of the Imperial Construction Administration and vice commissioner of Hu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: First in the jinshi, Construction vice director and Hu vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召試，改秘書省著作郎、直集賢院。

translations.literal: Summoned to examination, changed to Editorial Director of the Palace Library and straight collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: Examined, made Palace Library editorial director and Hall collator.

sentences.zh: 會從父沖坐事，出堯臣知光州。

translations.literal: When his father's cousin Chong was implicated in a case, Yaochen was sent out as Guang Prefecture prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Cousin Chong's case sent Yaochen out as Guang prefect.

sentences.zh: 父喪，服除，為三司度支判官，再遷右司諫。

translations.literal: Father mourning; after mourning ended he was Three Departments revenue judge and again promoted Right Secretariat remonstrator.
translations.idiomatic: After father mourning he was revenue judge, then Right Secretariat remonstrator.

sentences.zh: 郭皇后薨，議者歸罪內侍都知閻文應，堯臣請窮治左右侍醫者，不報。

translations.literal: When Empress Guo died, speakers blamed Inner Service director Yan Wenyin; Yaochen requested exhaustive trial of left and right attending physicians—no response.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Guo's death drew blame on Yan Wenyin; Yaochen sought trials of court physicians—ignored.

sentences.zh: 時上元節，有司張燈，堯臣俟乘輿出，即上言：“后已復位號，今方在殯，不當遊幸。”

translations.literal: At the time it was the Lantern Festival and offices hung lamps; Yaochen waited for the imperial carriage to go out and then memorialized: "The empress has already regained her title; now she lies in coffin—it is not fitting to tour."
translations.idiomatic: Lantern Festival: Yaochen stopped the emperor's outing while the empress still lay in coffin.

sentences.zh: 帝為罷張燈。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore abolished hanging lamps.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor canceled the lamps.

sentences.zh: 擢知制誥、同知通進銀臺司、提舉諸司庫務，知審刑院，入翰林為學士、知審官院。

translations.literal: Promoted edict drafter, concurrent Silver Terrace Memorial Office head, overseer of various storehouses, head of Judicial Review, entered Hanlin as academician and head of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted drafter, Silver Terrace head, storehouse overseer, Judicial Review head, Hanlin academician and Appointments head.

sentences.zh: 陜西用兵，為體量安撫使。

translations.literal: When Shaanxi used troops he was measurement-and-comfort commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi war made him measurement-and-comfort commissioner.

sentences.zh: 將行，請曰：“故事，使者所至，稱詔存問官吏將校，而不及於民。

translations.literal: About to depart he requested: "By precedent envoys wherever they go proclaim edicts to inquire after officials, generals, and clerks—but not the people.
translations.idiomatic: About to depart he requested: "By precedent envoys wherever they go proclaim edicts to officials, generals, and clerks—but not the people.

sentences.zh: 自元昊反，三年於今，關中之民雕弊為甚，請以詔勞來，仍諭以賊平蠲租賦二年。”

translations.literal: Since Yuan Hao rebelled three years to now, the people within the passes are greatly wasted; I request with an edict comfort them and still announce that when bandits are pacified rent and levies will be remitted two years."
translations.idiomatic: Since Yuan Hao rebelled three years ago, the people within the passes are greatly wasted; I request an edict to comfort them and announce that when bandits are pacified rent and levies will be remitted two years."

sentences.zh: 仁宗從之。

translations.literal: Renzong followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong agreed.

sentences.zh: 使還，上言：“陜西兵二十萬，分屯四路，然可使戰者止十萬。

translations.literal: On return he memorialized: "Shaanxi has two hundred thousand troops divided among four circuits, yet those who can fight are only one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On return he memorialized: "Shaanxi has two hundred thousand troops divided among four circuits, yet only one hundred thousand can fight.

sentences.zh: 賊眾入寇，常數倍官軍。

translations.literal: When bandits invade they are often several times government troops.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits often outnumbered government troops severalfold.

sentences.zh: 彼以十戰一，我以一戰十，故三至而三勝，由眾寡不侔也。

translations.literal: They fight one in ten battles; we fight ten in one—hence three arrivals and three victories, from unequal numbers.
translations.idiomatic: They chose one battle in ten; we one in ten—wins came from numbers.

sentences.zh: 涇原近賊巢穴，最當要害，宜先備之。

translations.literal: Jingyuan nears the bandit nest and is most strategically vital—it should be prepared first.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan near the enemy nest should be prepared first.

sentences.zh: 今防秋甚邇，請益團士兵，以二萬屯渭州，為鎮戎山外之援；

translations.literal: Now autumn defense is very near; I request increasing militia, stationing twenty thousand at Wei Prefecture as support beyond the mountains at Zhenrong;
translations.idiomatic: He sought twenty thousand militia at Wei for Zhenrong,

sentences.zh: 萬人屯涇州，為原、渭聲勢；

translations.literal: ten thousand at Jing Prefecture for Yuan and Wei momentum;
translations.idiomatic: ten thousand at Jing for Yuan-Wei support,

sentences.zh: 二萬屯環慶，萬人屯秦州，以制其沖突。

translations.literal: twenty thousand at Huanqing, ten thousand at Qin Prefecture, to check their thrusts.
translations.idiomatic: twenty thousand at Huanqing and ten thousand at Qin to block thrusts.

sentences.zh: 且賊之犯邊，不患不能入，患不能出也。

translations.literal: Moreover when bandits raid the border the worry is not that they cannot enter but that they cannot exit.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits' problem was leaving, not entering.

sentences.zh: 並塞地形，雖險易不同，而兵行須由大川，大川率有砦柵為控扼。

translations.literal: Along the border terrain though rugged and easy differ, army movement must follow great rivers, and great rivers mostly have forts and stockades for control.
translations.idiomatic: Armies had to follow rivers guarded by forts.

sentences.zh: 賊來利在虜掠，人自為戰，故所向無前。

translations.literal: When bandits come profit lies in barbarian plunder and each man fights for himself—hence they advance without obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders fought for plunder and advanced freely.

sentences.zh: 若延州之金明、塞門砦，鎮戎之劉璠、定川堡，渭州山外之羊牧隆城、靜邊砦，皆不能扼其來。

translations.literal: If at Yan Prefecture's Jinming and Saimen forts, Zhenrong's Liu Fan and Dingchuan forts, and beyond Wei mountains Yangmu Long city and Jingbian fort they cannot choke entry,
translations.idiomatic: Jinming, Saimen, Liu Fan, Dingchuan, Yangmu Long, and Jingbian could not block entry,

sentences.zh: 故賊不患不能入也。

translations.literal: then bandits need not fear inability to enter.
translations.idiomatic: so bandits entered easily.

sentences.zh: 既入漢地，分行鈔略，驅虜人畜，劫掠財貨，士馬疲困，奔趨歸路，無復鬥志。

translations.literal: Once within Han territory they divide to raid, drive off barbarians and livestock, plunder goods, and when men and horses are weary they rush the return road with no more will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Inside Han lands they raided until exhausted, then fled.

sentences.zh: 若以精兵扼險，強弩註射，旁設奇伏，斷其首尾，且追且擊，不敗何待。

translations.literal: If with picked troops you hold defiles, powerful crossbows shoot down, ambush is set on the flanks, and head and tail are cut while pursuing and striking, how could they not be defeated?
translations.idiomatic: Elite troops at defiles with crossbows and ambush could destroy retreating raiders.

sentences.zh: 故賊之患在不能出也。

translations.literal: Therefore the bandits' worry is inability to exit.
translations.idiomatic: Hence bandits feared not escaping.

sentences.zh: 賊屢乘戰勝，重掠而歸，諸將不能追擊者，由兵寡而勢分也。

translations.literal: Bandits often after repeated victories returned heavy with plunder and generals could not pursue because troops were few and momentum divided.
translations.idiomatic: Generals failed to pursue because troops were few and divided.

sentences.zh: 若尚循故轍，必無可勝之理。”

translations.literal: If we still follow the old rut there can be no principle of victory."
translations.idiomatic: If we still follow the old rut, there can be no principle of victory."

sentences.zh: 又論：“延州、鎮戎軍、渭州山外三敗之由，皆為賊先據勝地，誘致我師，將帥不能據險擊歸，而多倍道趨利。

translations.literal: He also discussed: "The reasons for the three defeats at Yan Prefecture, Zhenrong Army, and beyond Wei mountains were all that bandits first held advantageous ground and lured our armies; commanders could not hold defiles and strike returning troops but mostly took shortcuts for gain.
translations.idiomatic: He also discussed: "The reasons for the three defeats at Yan Prefecture, Zhenrong Army, and beyond Wei mountains were all that bandits first held advantageous ground and lured our armies; commanders could not hold defiles and strike returning troops but mostly took shortcuts for gain.

sentences.zh: 兵方疲頓，乃與生羌合戰；

translations.literal: When troops were already weary they joined battle with raw Qiang;
translations.idiomatic: Weary troops then fought Qiang allies;

sentences.zh: 賊始縱鐵騎沖我軍，繼以步卒挽強註射，鋒不可當，遂致掩覆，此主帥不思應變以懲前失之咎也。

translations.literal: bandits first loosed iron cavalry to charge our army, then infantry with strong bows shot down—the edge could not be faced, leading to envelopment and ruin—this is commanders not thinking to meet change and punish prior failure.
translations.idiomatic: iron cavalry and bow infantry overwhelmed unprepared commanders.

sentences.zh: 願敕邊吏，常遠斥候，遇賊至，度遠近立營砦，然後量敵奮擊，毋得輕出。”

translations.literal: I wish to order border officials always to scout far; when bandits come, gauge distance and establish camps and forts, then measure the enemy and strike boldly, not lightly going out."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to order border officials always to scout far; when bandits come, gauge distance and establish camps and forts, then measure the enemy and strike boldly, not lightly going out."

sentences.zh: 詔以其言戎邊吏。

translations.literal: An edict ordered his words passed to border officials.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent his advice to border officials.

sentences.zh: 時韓琦坐好水川兵敗徙秦州，范仲淹亦以擅復元昊書降耀州。

translations.literal: At the time Han Qi was moved to Qin Prefecture for the Haoshuichuan defeat and Fan Zhongyan was demoted to Yao Prefecture for restoring Yuan Hao's letter on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi was demoted after Haoshuichuan; Fan Zhongyan for answering Yuan Hao's letter.

sentences.zh: 堯臣言：“二人者，皆忠義智勇，不當置之散地。”

translations.literal: Yaochen said: "Both men are loyal, righteous, wise, and brave—they should not be placed in idle posts."
translations.idiomatic: Yaochen said both were loyal and capable and should not be sidelined.

sentences.zh: 又薦种世衡、狄青有將帥才。

translations.literal: He also recommended Chong Shihang and Di Qing had commanders' talent.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Chong Shihang and Di Qing as generals.

sentences.zh: 明年，賊果自鎮戎軍、原州入寇，敗葛懷敏，乘勝掠平涼、潘原，關中震恐，自邠、涇以東，皆閉壘自守。

translations.literal: The next year bandits indeed entered from Zhenrong Army and Yuan Prefecture, defeated Ge Huaimin, took advantage to plunder Pingliang and Panyuan—Guanzhong was terrified; from Bin and Jing east all closed forts and defended themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Next year raiders defeated Ge Huaimin and terrified Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 仲淹自將慶州兵捍賊，賊引去。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan personally led Qing Prefecture troops to block bandits; bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan blocked them and they withdrew.

sentences.zh: 仁宗思其言，乃復以琦、仲淹為招討使，置府涇州，益屯兵三萬人，而使堯臣再安撫涇原。

translations.literal: Renzong recalled his words and again made Qi and Fan pacification commissioners, established headquarters at Jing Prefecture, increased garrison by thirty thousand, and sent Yaochen again to comfort Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong restored Qi and Fan, added thirty thousand troops, and sent Yaochen to Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 初，曹瑋開山外地，置籠竿等四砦，募弓箭手，給田使耕戰自守。

translations.literal: At first Cao Wei opened lands beyond the mountains, established four forts such as Longgan, recruited archers, and allotted fields for farming and fighting self-defense.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei had opened frontier forts and archer-farmers.

sentences.zh: 其後將帥失撫禦，稍侵奪之，眾怨怒，遂劫德勝砦將姚貴，閉城畔。

translations.literal: Later commanders lost care; they were gradually encroached; the crowd resented and angrily seized Desheng Fort commander Yao Gui and closed the city in revolt.
translations.idiomatic: Later encroachment made archers seize Desheng Fort and rebel.

sentences.zh: 堯臣適過境上，作書射城中，諭以禍福，眾遂出降。

translations.literal: Yaochen happened to pass the border, wrote a letter shot into the city explaining fortune and calamity, and the crowd then came out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yaochen shot a letter into the city and secured surrender.

sentences.zh: 乃為申明約束如舊而去。

translations.literal: He then clarified constraints as before and departed.
translations.idiomatic: He restored old constraints and left.

sentences.zh: 既還，上言：“自陜西用兵，夏竦、陳執中並以兩府舊臣，為陜西經略、安撫、招討使，韓琦、范仲淹止為經略、安撫副使。

translations.literal: On return he memorialized: "Since Shaanxi used troops, Xia Song and Chen Zhizhong as old ministers of the two bureaus were Shaanxi overall pacification, comfort, and punitive commissioners; Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan were only vice pacification and comfort commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: On return he memorialized: "Since Shaanxi used troops, Xia Song and Chen Zhizhong as old ministers of the two bureaus were Shaanxi overall pacification, comfort, and punitive commissioners; Han Qi and Fan Zhongyan were only vice pacification and comfort commissioners.

sentences.zh: 既而張存知延州，王沿知渭州，張奎知慶州，俱是學士、待制之職，亦止管勾本路總管司事。

translations.literal: Later Zhang Cun governed Yan Prefecture, Wang Yan Wei Prefecture, Zhang Kui Qing Prefecture—all posts of academician or awaiting-formatter, also only managing their circuit overall command affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Later prefects were only circuit commanders in title.

sentences.zh: 及竦、執中罷，四路置帥，遂各帶都總管及經略、安撫、招討等使，因而武臣副總管亦為副使。

translations.literal: When Song and Chen were dismissed four circuits received commanders who each bore overall commander and pacification, comfort, and punitive titles, and military vice commanders also became vice commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: Four commanders then bore overlapping titles including military vice commissioners.

sentences.zh: 今琦、仲淹、龐籍既為陜西四路都總管、緣邊經略安撫招討等使，四路當稟節制，而尚帶經略使名者九人，各置司行事。

translations.literal: Now Qi, Fan, and Pang Ji are Shaanxi four-circuit overall commanders and frontier pacification, comfort, and punitive commissioners; the four circuits should obey direction, yet nine still bear pacification commissioner names, each establishing offices and acting.
translations.idiomatic: Nine pacification titles still duplicated command.

sentences.zh: 名號不異，而所稟非一。

translations.literal: Titles are not different yet what they obey is not one.
translations.idiomatic: Titles matched but authority did not.

sentences.zh: 今請逐路都總管、副總管並罷經略，只充緣邊安撫使。”

translations.literal: Now I request each circuit's overall and vice commanders all abolish pacification and serve only as frontier comfort commissioners."
translations.idiomatic: Now I request each circuit's overall and vice commanders all abolish pacification and serve only as frontier comfort commissioners."

sentences.zh: 既而滕宗諒亦以為請，遂罷之。

translations.literal: Soon Teng Zongliang also requested this and it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Teng Zongliang agreed and the titles were abolished.

sentences.zh: 又言：“鄜延、環慶路，其地皆險固而易守；

translations.literal: He also said: "Yan-Yan and Huanqing circuits—their lands are rugged and easy to defend;
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Yan-Yan and Huanqing circuits—their lands are rugged and easy to defend;

sentences.zh: 惟涇原自漢、唐以來，為沖要之地。

translations.literal: only Jingyuan from Han and Tang has been a vital point.
translations.idiomatic: only Jingyuan was vital since Han and Tang.

sentences.zh: 自鎮戎軍至渭州，沿涇河大川直抵涇、邠，略無險阻。

translations.literal: From Zhenrong Army to Wei Prefecture along the Jing River great passage straight to Jing and Bin there is scarcely rugged ground.
translations.idiomatic: From Zhenrong to Wei along the Jing River there was little rugged ground.

sentences.zh: 雖有城砦據平地，賊徑交屬，難以捍防，如郭子儀、渾瑊，常宿重兵守之。

translations.literal: Though there are forts on flat ground, bandit routes intersect and are hard to defend—as Guo Ziyi and Hun Zhen often stationed heavy troops.
translations.idiomatic: Flat forts were hard to defend—Guo Ziyi and Hun Zhen had garrisoned heavily.

sentences.zh: 自元昊叛命數年，由此三入寇。

translations.literal: Since Yuan Hao rebelled several years, through here he thrice invaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao had thrice invaded through Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 朝廷置帥府於涇州，為控扼關、陜之會，誠合事機。

translations.literal: The court placed headquarters at Jing Prefecture to control the meeting of Guan and Shaanxi—truly fitting circumstance.
translations.idiomatic: Jing headquarters rightly controlled Guan-Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 然頻經敗覆，邊地空虛，士氣不振。

translations.literal: Yet after repeated defeats the border was empty and morale unsteady.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated defeats had emptied the border and morale.

sentences.zh: 願深監近弊，精擇將佐；

translations.literal: I wish deep scrutiny of recent abuses and careful selection of assistants;
translations.idiomatic: He urged scrutiny of abuses and better generals;

sentences.zh: 其新集之兵，未經訓練，宜易以舊人。

translations.literal: the newly gathered troops untrained should be exchanged for old hands.
translations.idiomatic: untrained new troops should be replaced by veterans.

sentences.zh: 儻一路兵力完實，則賊不敢長驅入寇矣。”

translations.literal: If one circuit's military strength were complete and solid, bandits would not dare long-drive invasion."
translations.idiomatic: If one circuit's military strength were complete and solid, bandits would not dare long-drive invasion."

sentences.zh: 因論沿邊城砦、控扼要害、賊徑通屬及備禦輕重之策為五事上之。

translations.literal: He therefore discussed frontier forts, controlling strategic points, bandit route connections, and defensive weight in five items and submitted them.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted five frontier defense proposals.

sentences.zh: 又請涇、原五州營田，益置弓箭手，及請徹潼關樓櫓，皆報可。

translations.literal: He also requested Jingyuan five prefectures' military colonies, increasing archers, and removing Tong Pass towers—all approved.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan colony troops, more archers, and removing Tong towers were approved.

sentences.zh: 以戶部郎中權三司使，辟張溫之、杜杞等十余人為副使、判官。

translations.literal: As Revenue Section director acting Three Departments commissioner he recruited Zhang Wenzhi, Du Qi, and more than ten others as vice commissioners and judges.
translations.idiomatic: As acting Three Departments commissioner he recruited Zhang Wenzhi, Du Qi, and ten others.

sentences.zh: 時入內都知張永和建議，收民僦舍錢十之三以助軍費。

translations.literal: At the time Inner Attendant director Zhang Yonghe proposed collecting three-tenths of civilian lease money to aid military expense.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yonghe proposed taking three-tenths of lease money for the army.

sentences.zh: 堯臣入對曰：“此衰世之事，召怨而攜民，唐德宗所以致朱泚之亂也。”

translations.literal: Yaochen answered: "This is a matter of a declining age, inviting resentment and alienating the people—Tang Dezong thereby brought Zhu Ci's disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Yaochen called it a declining-age policy that would bring Zhu Ci-style revolt.

sentences.zh: 度支副使林濰畏永和，附會其說，堯臣奏黜濰，議乃定。

translations.literal: Revenue vice commissioner Lin Wei feared Yonghe and joined his view; Yaochen memorialized to dismiss Wei and the debate was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Lin Wei sided with Yonghe; Yaochen dismissed Wei and ended the plan.

sentences.zh: 夔州轉運使請增鹽井歲課十餘萬緡，堯臣以為上恩未嘗及遠人，而反牟取厚利，適足以斂怨，罷之。

translations.literal: Kuizhou transport commissioner requested increasing salt-well yearly levy by more than a hundred thousand strings; Yaochen thought the emperor's grace had not reached distant people yet they would instead seek thick profit, enough to gather resentment, and abolished it.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked a Kuizhou salt-well tax hike as exploitative.

sentences.zh: 遷翰林學士承旨兼端明殿學士，為群牧使。

translations.literal: Promoted chief Hanlin academician with Illustrious Hall academician and Herds commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted chief Hanlin academician, Illustrious Hall academician, Herds commissioner.

sentences.zh: 丁母喪，服除，轉右諫議大夫。

translations.literal: Mother mourning; after mourning ended changed to Right Remonstrance Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After mother mourning, Right Remonstrance Censor.

sentences.zh: 初，學士蘇易簡、丁度皆自郎中進中書舍人充承旨，及堯臣為承旨，不遷官，意宰相賈昌朝所抑。

translations.literal: At first academicians Su Yijian and Ding Du were both promoted from director to Secretariat drafting attendant as chief academician; when Yaochen was chief academician he was not promoted in office—he thought chief minister Jia Changchao had suppressed him.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yijian and Ding Du had been promoted as chief academician; Yaochen blamed Jia Changchao for blocking him.

sentences.zh: 及是，文彥博為相，因其歲滿，遂優遷之。

translations.literal: At this time Wen Yanbo was chief minister; because his term was complete he was favorably promoted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wen Yanbo became chief minister, Yaochen was favorably promoted at term's end.

sentences.zh: 大享明堂，加給事中。

translations.literal: At the great Bright Hall sacrifice added Supervising Censor.
translations.idiomatic: At the Bright Hall sacrifice he was made Supervising Censor.

sentences.zh: 與三司更議茶法，較天下每歲財賦出入，上其數，遂拜樞密副使。

translations.literal: With the Three Departments he reconsidered tea law, compared yearly revenue in and out nationwide, submitted the figures, and was appointed Military Affairs vice commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He reworked tea law, tallied national revenue, and became Military Affairs vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 會儂智高反，請析廣西宜、容、邕州為三路，以融、柳、象隸宜州，白、高、竇、雷、化、郁林、儀、藤、梧、龔、瓊隸容州，欽、賓、廉、橫、潯、貴隸邕州；

translations.literal: When Nong Zhigao rebelled he requested dividing Guangxi Yi, Rong, and Yong prefectures into three circuits—Rong, Liu, and Xiang subordinate to Yi; Bai, Gao, Dou, Lei, Hua, Yulin, Yi, Teng, Wu, Gong, and Qiong subordinate to Rong; Qin, Bin, Lian, Heng, Xun, and Gui subordinate to Yong;
translations.idiomatic: Nong Zhigao's rebellion led him to split Guangxi into three circuits with listed prefectures.

sentences.zh: 遇蠻入寇，三路會支郡兵掩擊，令經略、安撫使守桂州以統制焉；

translations.literal: when barbarians invaded the three circuits would jointly strike with branch-prefecture troops, ordering pacification and comfort commissioners to hold Guilin for overall control;
translations.idiomatic: barbarian raids would draw joint strikes under a Guilin commissioner;

sentences.zh: 益募澄海、忠敢土軍分屯，運全、永、道三州米以餉之，罷遣北兵遠戍。

translations.literal: increase recruiting Chenghai and Zhonggan native troops for garrison, transport grain from Quan, Yong, and Dao to supply them, and dismiss northern troops far garrisoned.
translations.idiomatic: recruit native troops, ship grain from three prefectures, and recall northern garrisons.

sentences.zh: 時狄青經制嶺南，詔青審議，以為便。

translations.literal: At the time Di Qing overall administered Lingnan; an edict ordered Qing to review and he said it was convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Di Qing approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 居樞密三年，務裁抑僥幸，於是有鏤匿名書以布京城，然仁宗不以為疑也。

translations.literal: Three years in Military Affairs he strove to curb favor-seeking; thereupon anonymous letters carved and posted appeared in the capital—yet Renzong did not suspect him.
translations.idiomatic: Three years curbing favoritism brought anonymous posters, but Renzong did not suspect him.

sentences.zh: 以戶部侍郎參知政事。

translations.literal: As Revenue Section director he was appointed Vice Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: As Revenue director he became Vice Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 久之，帝欲以為樞密使，而當制學士胡宿固抑之，乃進吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: After long time the emperor wished to make him Military Affairs commissioner, but drafting academician Hu Su firmly suppressed it; he was therefore promoted Personnel vice minister.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wanted him as Military Affairs commissioner; Hu Su blocked it and he became Personnel vice minister.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈尚書左僕射，謚文安。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously made Left Vice Director of the Secretariat, posthumous title Wen'an.
translations.idiomatic: He died; posthumously Left Secretariat vice director, posthumous Wen'an.

sentences.zh: 堯臣以文學進，典內外制十餘年，其為文辭溫麗。

translations.literal: Yaochen advanced through literature, managed inner and outer edicts more than ten years; his literary compositions were warm and beautiful.
translations.idiomatic: A literary man, he drafted edicts over ten years in warm, polished prose.

sentences.zh: 執政時，嘗與宰相文彥博、富弼、劉沆勸帝早立嗣，且言英宗嘗養宮中，宜為後，為詔草挾以進，未果立。

translations.literal: While in governance he once with chief ministers Wen Yanbo, Fu Bi, and Liu Hang urged the emperor early to establish an heir, saying Yingzong had been raised in the palace and should succeed, drafting an edict and carrying it to present—yet establishment did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: In office he urged an early heir, favoring palace-raised Yingzong, but the edict failed.

sentences.zh: 元豐三年，子同老進遺稿論父功，帝以訪文彥博，具奏本末，遂加贈太師、中書令，改謚文忠。

translations.literal: In Yuanfeng year three son Tonglao presented leftover drafts discussing his father's merit; the emperor consulted Wen Yanbo, who fully memorialized the sequence; thereupon added posthumous Grand Tutor and Secretariat Director, changed posthumous title to Wenzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanfeng year three his son secured posthumous Grand Tutor and Secretariat Director and posthumous Wenzhong.

sentences.zh: 孫抃，字夢得，眉州眉山人。

translations.literal: Sun Bian, style name Mengde, was a man of Meishan, Mei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Bian, styled Mengde, of Meishan in Mei Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六世祖長孺，喜藏書，號“書樓孫氏”，子孫以田為業。

translations.literal: Sixth-generation ancestor Changru loved collecting books, styled "Sun Clan of the Book Tower"; descendants took farming as their occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestor Changru collected books as the Book Tower Suns; later kin farmed.

sentences.zh: 至抃始讀書屬文。

translations.literal: Only with Bian did reading and composing begin.
translations.idiomatic: Bian was the first literatus in the line.

sentences.zh: 中進士甲科，以大理評事通判絳州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi top grade and was made reviewer of the Court of Judicial Review and vice commissioner of Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Top-grade jinshi, Judicial Review reviewer and Jiang vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 召試學士院，除太常丞、直集賢院，為開封府推官，判三司開拆司，同修起居注，以右正言知制誥，遷起居舍人、翰林學士兼侍讀學士、史館修撰，累遷尚書吏部郎中。

translations.literal: Summoned to the Hanlin examination, made Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Administration and straight collator of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, Kaifeng investigating officer, judge of the Three Departments opening office, co-compiler of Daily Records, as Right Rectifier and edict drafter, promoted Drafting Gentleman, Hanlin academician with Attendant Reader and Historiography reviser, repeatedly promoted Personnel Section director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Hanlin exam, Sacrifices vice director, Hall collator, Kaifeng investigator, Daily Records co-compiler, drafter, Hanlin academician, Attendant Reader, Historiography reviser, Personnel Section director.

sentences.zh: 抃雖久處顯要，罕所建明。

translations.literal: Though Bian long held eminent posts he seldom proposed or clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Despite long prominence Bian seldom proposed policy.

sentences.zh: 皇祐中，以右諫議大夫權御史中丞。

translations.literal: In Huangyou he was Right Remonstrance Censor acting Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Huangyou year he acted as Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 制下，諫官韓絳論奏抃非糾繩才，不可任風憲。
