translations.literal: When the order descended remonstrance official Han Jiang memorialized that Bian lacked talent for correction and could not bear the censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang said Bian lacked censorial talent.

sentences.zh: 抃即手疏曰：“臣觀方今士人，趨進者多，廉退者少。

translations.literal: Bian immediately wrote by hand: "Your servant observes that among present scholars many rush advancement and few are modest in retreat.
translations.idiomatic: Bian immediately wrote by hand: "Your servant observes that among present scholars many rush advancement and few are modest in retreat.

sentences.zh: 以善求事為精神，以能訐人為風采；

translations.literal: Taking skill in seeking affairs as spirit, taking ability to denounce people as style;
translations.idiomatic: They prized scheming and denunciation;

sentences.zh: 捷給若嗇夫者謂之有議論，刻深若酷吏者謂之有政事。

translations.literal: the quick-tongued like a miser are called having discourse; the harsh like a cruel official are called having governance.
translations.idiomatic: quick tongues passed for debate, harshness for governance.

sentences.zh: 諫官所謂才者，無乃謂是乎？

translations.literal: Is the talent remonstrance officials speak of not this?
translations.idiomatic: Is that the talent you mean?

sentences.zh: 若然，臣誠不能也。”

translations.literal: If so, your servant truly cannot."
translations.idiomatic: If so, your servant truly cannot."

sentences.zh: 仁宗察其言，趣視事，且命知審官院。

translations.literal: Renzong perceived his meaning, hastened him to take office, and ordered him to head the Court of Appointments.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong read his intent, ordered him to work, and named him Appointments head.

sentences.zh: 抃辭以任言責不當兼事局，乃止。

translations.literal: Bian declined that bearing remonstrance responsibility he should not concurrently hold bureau affairs, and it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He declined a concurrent bureau post.

sentences.zh: 在臺，數言事，不為矯激，尤喜稱薦人才。

translations.literal: In the Censorate he often spoke on affairs, not exaggeratedly harsh, and especially loved praising and recommending talent.
translations.idiomatic: As censor he spoke moderately and recommended talent.

sentences.zh: 帝欲除入內都知王守忠領武寧軍節度使，抃奏罷之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to make Inner Attendant director Wang Shouzhong hold Wuning military commissioner; Bian memorialized and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: He blocked Wang Shouzhong from a military commission.

sentences.zh: 溫成皇后葬，以劉沆為監護使，抃奏沆為宰相，不當為后妃護葬喪事。

translations.literal: When Empress Wencheng was buried Liu Hang was made oversight commissioner; Bian memorialized that Hang as chief minister should not oversee empress burial.
translations.idiomatic: He objected to chief minister Liu Hang overseeing Wencheng's burial.

sentences.zh: 時又議為后建陵立廟，抃率官屬言非禮。

translations.literal: At the time they also debated building a tomb and temple for the empress; Bian led officials to say it was not ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He led officials against a tomb and temple as unritual.

sentences.zh: 因相與請對，固爭不能得，伏地不起，帝為改容遣之。

translations.literal: They therefore together requested audience and firmly argued without success, prostrating and not rising; the emperor changed expression and sent them away.
translations.idiomatic: They prostrated themselves until the emperor relented.

sentences.zh: 御史請罷宰相梁適，未聽，抃奏曰：“適在相位，上不能持平權衡，下不能篤訓子弟。

translations.literal: Censors requested dismissing chief minister Liang Shi; not heard; Bian memorialized: "Shi in the chief post above cannot balance the scales, below cannot earnestly teach sons and younger brothers.
translations.idiomatic: Censors requested dismissing chief minister Liang Shi; not heard; Bian memorialized: "Shi in the chief post above cannot balance the scales, below cannot earnestly teach sons and younger brothers.

sentences.zh: 言事官數論奏，未聞報可，非罷適無以慰物論。”

translations.literal: Remonstrance officials repeatedly memorialized without response heard—unless Shi is dismissed popular opinion cannot be comforted."
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance officials repeatedly memorialized without response heard—unless Shi is dismissed popular opinion cannot be comforted."

sentences.zh: 宰相陳執中婢為嬖妾張氏榜殺，置獄取證左，執中弗遣，有詔勿推。

translations.literal: Chief minister Chen Zhizhong's maid was beaten to death by favored concubine Zhang; prison was set to take witnesses but Zhizhong would not send them; there was an edict not to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhizhong blocked investigation of a maid killed by his concubine.

sentences.zh: 抃復與官屬請對論列，疏十上，適、執中卒皆罷。

translations.literal: Bian again with officials requested audience to argue; ten memorials—Shi and Zhizhong in the end were both dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Ten memorials later Liang Shi and Chen Zhizhong fell.

sentences.zh: 改翰林學士承旨，復兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Changed to chief Hanlin academician, again concurrently Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: Made chief Hanlin academician and Attendant Reader.

sentences.zh: 帝讀《史記‧龜策傳》，問：“古人動作必由此乎？”

translations.literal: The emperor read the 《Records of the Grand Historian: Divination by Tortoise》, and asked: "Did ancients in action always follow this?"
translations.idiomatic: Reading 《Records: Divination by Tortoise》, he asked if ancients always divined.

sentences.zh: 對曰：“古有大疑，既決於己，又詢於眾，猶謂不有天命乎，於是命龜以斷吉兇。

translations.literal: He replied: "In antiquity when there was great doubt, after deciding in oneself one also consulted the multitude; still thinking there might be no Heaven's mandate, one then ordered tortoise to decide fortune and calamity.
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "In antiquity when there was great doubt, after deciding in oneself one also consulted the multitude; still thinking there might be no Heaven's mandate, one then ordered tortoise to decide fortune and calamity.

sentences.zh: 所謂‘謀及乃心，謀及卿士，謀及庶人，謀及卜筮’。

translations.literal: What is called 'consult one's heart, consult ministers and grandees, consult the multitude, consult divination.'
translations.idiomatic: That is consulting heart, ministers, people, and divination.

sentences.zh: 蓋聖人貴誠，不專人謀，默與神契，然後為得也。”

translations.literal: Sages value sincerity, not specializing in human counsel alone, silently matching the divine—then it is obtained."
translations.idiomatic: Sages value sincerity, not specializing in human counsel alone, silently matching the divine—then it is obtained."

sentences.zh: 帝善其對。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his reply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 諫官陳升之上選用、責任、考課轉運使三法，命抃與御史中丞張升典之，卒亦無所進退焉。

translations.literal: Remonstrance official Chen Shengzhi submitted three laws on selection, responsibility, and evaluation of transport commissioners; the emperor ordered Bian with Vice Censor-in-Chief Zhang Sheng to preside—in the end there was neither promotion nor demotion.
translations.idiomatic: He and Zhang Sheng presided over transport reforms with no result.

sentences.zh: 再遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: Again promoted Vice Rites Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted Vice Rites Minister.

sentences.zh: 抃久居侍從，泊如也，人以為長者。

translations.literal: Bian long dwelt in attendance, tranquil as if nothing; people regarded him as an elder.
translations.idiomatic: Long in attendance, tranquil, he was seen as an elder.

sentences.zh: 既而樞密副使程戡罷，帝欲用舊人，即以命抃。

translations.literal: Later Military Affairs vice commissioner Cheng Kan was dismissed; the emperor wished to use an old hand and with this order appointed Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng Kan left, Renzong appointed the veteran Bian.

sentences.zh: 歲中，參知政事。

translations.literal: Within the year Vice Participant in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he became Vice Participant in Governance.

sentences.zh: 抃性篤厚寡言，質略無威儀。

translations.literal: Bian's nature was sincere and thick, sparing of words, plain and without imposing ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere, taciturn, plain, without ceremony.

sentences.zh: 居兩府，年益耄，無所可否。

translations.literal: In the two bureaus, years increasingly aged, he neither affirmed nor denied.
translations.idiomatic: In the two bureaus he aged and neither affirmed nor denied.

sentences.zh: 又善忘，語言舉止多可笑，好事者至傳以為口實。

translations.literal: Also good at forgetting; speech and conduct were often laughable—those who loved tales even spread them as material.
translations.idiomatic: Forgetful and often ridiculous, he became gossip.

sentences.zh: 御史韓縝彈奏之，罷為觀文殿學士、同群牧制置使，復兼侍讀學士。

translations.literal: Censor Han Zong impeached him; dismissed as Observant Culture academician, concurrent Herds commissioner, again Attendant Reader.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zong impeached him; he became Observant Culture academician and Herds commissioner.

sentences.zh: 英宗即位，進戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Yingzong acceded promoted Revenue Section director.
translations.idiomatic: Yingzong made him Revenue Section director.

sentences.zh: 告老，以太子少傅就第，卒。

translations.literal: He requested retirement; as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent he took his residence and died.
translations.idiomatic: He retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and died.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚文懿。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Wenyi.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous Wenyi.

sentences.zh: 田況，字元均，其先冀州信都人。

translations.literal: Tian Kuang, style name Yuanjun, his ancestors were people of Xindu, Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Kuang, styled Yuanjun, from Xindu in Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 晉亂，祖行周沒於契丹。

translations.literal: In Jin disorder grandfather Xingzhou died among the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Grandfather Xingzhou died among Khitan in Jin turmoil.

sentences.zh: 父延昭，景德中脫身南歸，性沈鷙，教子甚嚴，累官至太子率府率。

translations.literal: Father Yanzhao in Jingde escaped south; nature deep and fierce, teaching sons very strict, repeatedly rose to Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Escort.
translations.idiomatic: Father Yanzhao escaped south in Jingde, strict, rose to Heir Apparent Escort commandant.

sentences.zh: 況少卓犖有大志，好讀書。

translations.literal: Kuang in youth was outstanding with great ambition and loved reading.
translations.idiomatic: Youthful Kuang was ambitious and bookish.

sentences.zh: 舉進士甲科，補江陵府推官，再調楚州判官，遷秘書省著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi top grade and was appointed push officer of Jiangling Prefecture, again transferred as judge of Chu Prefecture, promoted Editorial Assistant of the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Top-grade jinshi, Jiangling push officer, Chu judge, Palace Library editorial assistant.

sentences.zh: 舉賢良方正，改太常丞、通判江寧府。

translations.literal: Passed worthy and upright examination, changed to Vice Director of the Imperial Sacrifices Administration and vice commissioner of Jiangning Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Worthy-and-upright exam, Sacrifices vice director, Jiangning vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 趙元昊反，夏竦經略陜西，辟為判官。

translations.literal: When Zhao Yuanhao rebelled Xia Song overall administered Shaanxi and recruited him as judge.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanhao's rebellion brought him to Xia Song's Shaanxi staff.

sentences.zh: 時竦與韓琦、尹洙等畫上攻守二策，朝廷將用攻策，范仲淹議未可出師。

translations.literal: At the time Song with Han Qi, Yin Zhu, and others drafted attack and defense strategies; the court was about to use the attack plan while Fan Zhongyan argued troops should not yet go out.
translations.idiomatic: Song, Han Qi, and Yin Zhu favored attack; Fan Zhongyan opposed.

sentences.zh: 況上疏曰：“昔繼遷擾邊，太宗部分諸將五路進討，或遇賊不擊，或戰衄而還。

translations.literal: Kuang memorialized: "Formerly when Jiqian disturbed the border Taizong divided generals on five routes to attack; some met bandits and did not strike, some fought and retreated defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang memorialized: "Formerly when Jiqian disturbed the border Taizong divided generals on five routes to attack; some met bandits and did not strike, some fought and retreated defeated.

sentences.zh: 又嘗令白守素、馬紹忠護送糧餉於靈州，諸將多違詔自奮，浦洛河之敗，死者數萬人。

translations.literal: Again he ordered Bai Shousu and Ma Shaozhong to escort grain to Ling Prefecture; many generals disobeyed the edict and acted on their own—the Pulu River defeat killed tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Pulu River disaster killed tens of thousands when generals disobeyed.

sentences.zh: 今將帥士卒，素已懦怯，未甚更練。

translations.literal: Now commanders and soldiers are by nature already cowardly and have not been much more trained.
translations.idiomatic: Today's commanders and troops were untrained cowards.

sentences.zh: 又知韓琦、尹洙同建此策，恐未甚稟服，臨事進退，有誤大舉。

translations.literal: Also knowing Han Qi and Yin Zhu together made this plan, I fear they are not much obedient—in the event advance and retreat err and harm the great undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: Han Qi and Yin Zhu might not obey, ruining the campaign.

sentences.zh: 其不可一也。

translations.literal: This is the first impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: First impossibility.

sentences.zh: 計者以為賊常並力而來，我常分兵以禦，眾寡不敵，多貽敗衄，今若全師大舉，必有成功，此思之未熟爾。

translations.literal: Planners think bandits always come with combined strength while we always divide troops to defend—unequal numbers, many defeats; now if the whole army advances greatly there must be success—this is thinking not mature.
translations.idiomatic: Mass assault seems wise only if immature.

sentences.zh: 夫三軍之命，系於將帥。

translations.literal: The fate of the three armies hangs on commanders.
translations.idiomatic: Armies depend on commanders.

sentences.zh: 人之才有大小，智有遠近，以漢祖之善將，不若淮陰之益辦，況庸人乎？

translations.literal: Men's talent has large and small, wisdom near and far—even Han Gaozu's skill in commanding is not like Huaiyin's greater capacity, how much less ordinary men?
translations.idiomatic: Even Han Gaozu was no Huaiyin—lesser commanders were riskier.

sentences.zh: 今徙知大眾可以威敵，而不思將帥之才否，此禍之大者也。

translations.literal: Now planners know great masses can awe enemies but do not consider whether commanders have talent—this is a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Mass alone without talented commanders was calamity.

sentences.zh: 兩路之人，眾十餘萬，庸將驅之，若為舒卷；

translations.literal: People of two circuits, masses of more than a hundred thousand, driven by mediocre generals as if rolling and unrolling;
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand on two circuits under mediocre generals were unwieldy;

sentences.zh: 賊若據險設伏，邀截沖擊，首尾前後，勢不相援，一有不利，則邊防莫守，別貽後患。

translations.literal: if bandits hold defiles and set ambush, intercept and strike, head, tail, before and after cannot support each other—once disadvantage appears the border cannot be held and other troubles are left.
translations.idiomatic: ambush could shatter them and leave the border bare.

sentences.zh: 安危之計，決於一舉。

translations.literal: Safety and danger decided in one throw.
translations.idiomatic: Safety hung on one throw.

sentences.zh: 其不可二也。

translations.literal: This is the second impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Second impossibility.

sentences.zh: 自西賊叛命以來，雖屢乘機會，然終不敢深寇郡縣，以厭其欲者，非算之少也。

translations.literal: Since western bandits rebelled, though often seizing opportunity they ultimately did not dare deeply raid commanderies and counties to satisfy desire—not from little planning.
translations.idiomatic: Raiders had not deep-raided despite chances—not from lack of plans.

sentences.zh: 直以中國之大，賢俊之盛，甲兵之眾，未易可測。

translations.literal: Simply because China's greatness, worthies' abundance, and armor's multitude were not easy to measure.
translations.idiomatic: They feared China's size, talent, and arms.

sentences.zh: 今師深入，若無成功，挫國威靈，為賊輕侮，或別墮奸計，以致他虞。

translations.literal: Now if the army enters deeply without success, national prestige is wounded, bandits lightly insult, or separately fall into treacherous plots leading to other worries.
translations.idiomatic: Deep failure would wound prestige or invite traps.

sentences.zh: 其不可三也。

translations.literal: This is the third impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Third impossibility.

sentences.zh: 計者又云，將帥雖未足倚，下流勇進，或有其人。

translations.literal: Planners also say though commanders cannot be relied on, lower ranks bravely advancing may have men.
translations.idiomatic: Some hoped brave subordinates might succeed.

sentences.zh: 自劉平、石元孫陷沒，士氣挫怯，未能振起。

translations.literal: Since Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun were lost morale was wounded and timid, unable to rouse.
translations.idiomatic: Since Liu Ping and Shi Yuansun morale had not recovered.

sentences.zh: 今兵數雖多，疲懦者眾，以庸將驅怯兵，入不測之地，獨其下使臣數輩，幹賞蹈利，欲邀奇功，未見其利。

translations.literal: Now though troops are many, the weary and cowardly are many; mediocre generals driving timid soldiers into unknown lands—only a few lower envoys seeking merit and profit wish strange achievement; their benefit is not seen.
translations.idiomatic: Many troops were weary cowards led by mediocrity for petty glory.

sentences.zh: 其不可四也。

translations.literal: This is the fourth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth impossibility.

sentences.zh: 計者又云，非欲深絕沙磧，以窮妖巢，但淺入山界，以挫賊氣，如襲白豹城之比。

translations.literal: Planners also say they do not wish deeply to end the sands and exhaust the demon nest but shallowly enter mountain borders to blunt bandit spirit, like raiding Baicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Shallow raids like Baicheng were proposed.

sentences.zh: 臣謂乘虛襲掠，既不能破戎首、拉兇黨，但殘戮孥弱，以厚怨毒，非王師吊伐招徠之體。

translations.literal: Your servant thinks seizing emptiness to raid cannot break the barbarian chief or pull down fierce cliques but only slaughter the weak and deepen hatred—not the royal army's style of punitive expedition and summoning.
translations.idiomatic: Raiding women and children was not royal punitive style.

sentences.zh: 然事出無策，為彼之所為，亦當霆發雷逝，往來輕速，以掩其不備。

translations.literal: Yet when affairs leave no stratagem and one does as they do, one should also burst like thunder and come and go light and fast to catch them unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: If raiding, it must be swift surprise.

sentences.zh: 今興師十萬，鼓行而西，賊已清野據險以待，我師何襲挫之有？

translations.literal: Now raising a hundred thousand troops marching west, bandits have cleared fields and hold defiles to wait—what surprise defeat can our army have?
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand marching west met prepared enemies—no surprise.

sentences.zh: 其不可五也。

translations.literal: This is the fifth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth impossibility.

sentences.zh: 自元昊寇邊，人皆知其誅賞明、計數黠。

translations.literal: Since Yuan Hao raided the border people all know his rewards and punishments are clear and schemes crafty.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Hao was known for clear discipline and crafty schemes.

sentences.zh: 今未有間隙可窺，而暴為興舉，計事者但欲決勝負於一戰。

translations.literal: Now there is no gap to spy yet suddenly a great undertaking—planners only wish to decide victory and defeat in one battle.
translations.idiomatic: No gap existed yet planners wanted one decisive battle.

sentences.zh: 幸其或有所成，否則願自比王恢以待罪，勇則勇矣，如國事何。

translations.literal: Fortunate if something succeeds; otherwise willing to compare themselves to Wang Hui awaiting punishment—brave indeed, but what of state affairs?
translations.idiomatic: Brave like Wang Hui awaiting punishment, but state affairs suffered.

sentences.zh: 其不可六也。

translations.literal: This is the sixth impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Sixth impossibility.

sentences.zh: 昨仲淹奏乞朝廷，敦包荒之量，存鄜延一路。

translations.literal: Earlier Fan Zhongyan memorialized begging the court to cherish vast forbearance and preserve the Yan-Yan route.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan had urged preserving the Yan-Yan route.

sentences.zh: 今諸將勒兵嚴備，未行討伐，容示以恩意，歲時之間，或可招納。

translations.literal: Now generals restrain troops in strict preparation without yet launching attack, showing grace—in yearly time perhaps they can be enticed.
translations.idiomatic: Strict defense might entice peace without attack.

sentences.zh: 若使涇原一路獨入，則孤軍進退，憂患不淺。

translations.literal: If only Jingyuan circuit enters alone then a lone army's advance and retreat has no shallow worry.
translations.idiomatic: Jingyuan alone would be dangerously isolated.

sentences.zh: 傳聞賊謀，俟我師諸路入界，並兵以敵，此正陷賊計中。

translations.literal: Rumored bandit plot waits for our armies of all routes to enter borders then combines troops to oppose—this is exactly falling into bandit calculation.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits would unite when all routes entered—seventh trap.

sentences.zh: 其不可七也。

translations.literal: This is the seventh impossibility.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh impossibility.

sentences.zh: 以臣所見，夏竦、韓琦、尹洙同獻此策，今若奏乞中罷，則是自相違異；

translations.literal: In your servant's view Xia Song, Han Qi, and Yin Zhu together presented this plan; now if memorializing to stop midway then it is self-contradiction;
translations.idiomatic: Stopping now would contradict Song, Han Qi, and Yin Zhu;

sentences.zh: 欲果決進討，則又仲淹執議不同。

translations.literal: if wishing to decide and advance attack then again Fan Zhongyan holds different discussion.
translations.idiomatic: attacking would oppose Fan Zhongyan.

sentences.zh: 乞召兩府大臣定議，但令嚴設邊備，若有侵掠，即出兵邀擊；

translations.literal: I beg summon two-bureau chief ministers to fix discussion, only strictly set border defense—if there is plunder then send troops to intercept;
translations.idiomatic: He urged chief ministers to fortify borders and intercept only raids;

sentences.zh: 或賊界謹自守備，不必先用輕舉。

translations.literal: or if bandit territory carefully self-defends, need not first use light undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: not rash campaigns.

sentences.zh: 如此則全威制勝，有功而無患也。”

translations.literal: Thus full prestige controls victory with achievement and no worry."
translations.idiomatic: Thus full prestige controls victory with achievement and no worry."

sentences.zh: 於是罷出師議。

translations.literal: Thereupon the outbound army debate was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign was canceled.

sentences.zh: 況又言治邊十四事。

translations.literal: Kuang also memorialized fourteen items on governing the border.
translations.idiomatic: He also submitted fourteen border reforms.

sentences.zh: 遷右正言，管勾國子監、判三司理欠憑由司，專供諫職，權修起居注，遂知制誥。

translations.literal: Promoted Right Rectifier, oversaw the Directorate of Education, judged the Three Departments arrears voucher office, specialized in remonstrance duties, acting compiler of Daily Records, then edict drafter.
translations.idiomatic: Right Rectifier, Education overseer, arrears judge, remonstrator, Daily Records compiler, drafter.

sentences.zh: 嘗面奏事，論及政體，帝頗以好名為非，意在遵守故常，況退而著論上之。

translations.literal: He once memorialized in person discussing government structure; the emperor rather took love of name as fault, intent on keeping old constants; Kuang on withdrawal composed a discourse and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Renzong disliked name-seeking; Kuang wrote a rebuttal.

sentences.zh: 其略曰：“名者由實而生，非徒好而自至也。

translations.literal: The summary said: "Name is born from substance, not merely loving it and it comes of itself.
translations.idiomatic: The summary said: "Name is born from substance, not merely loving it and it comes of itself.

sentences.zh: 堯、舜三代之君，非好名者。

translations.literal: Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties rulers were not lovers of name.
translations.idiomatic: Yao, Shun, and Three Dynasties rulers did not chase names.

sentences.zh: 而鴻烈休德，倬若日月，不能纖晦者，有實美而然也。

translations.literal: Yet their grand virtue was lofty as sun and moon and could not be slightly hidden—because there was real beauty and thus.
translations.idiomatic: Real virtue shone like the sun.

sentences.zh: 設或謙弱自守，不為恢閎睿明之事，則名從而晦矣，雖欲好之，豈可得耶。

translations.literal: Suppose one is modest and self-guarding, not doing expansive and discerning bright affairs, then name follows and is hidden—though wishing to love it, how could it be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: Modesty without great deeds hides name despite desire.

sentences.zh: 方今政令寬弛，百職不修，二虜熾結，淩慢中國，朝廷恫矜下民橫罹殺掠，竭瀝膏血，以資繕備，而未免侵軼之憂。

translations.literal: Present government orders are lax, hundred offices unrepaired, the two barbarians blaze and knot, insulting China; the court pities the people below suffering slaughter and plunder, draining marrow and blood to fund repairs, yet still cannot avoid raid worry.
translations.idiomatic: Lax government, unrepaired offices, barbarian insults, and costly defense still failed.

sentences.zh: 故屈就講和，為翕張予奪之術。

translations.literal: Therefore bending to peace talks is a technique of tightening and loosening, granting and taking.
translations.idiomatic: Peace talks were a grant-and-withhold tactic.

sentences.zh: 自非君臣朝夕恥憤，大有為以遏後虞，則勢可憂矣。

translations.literal: Unless ruler and ministers daily feel shame and anger and greatly act to check later worry, the situation can be worrisome.
translations.idiomatic: Without shame and bold action, peril loomed.

sentences.zh: 陛下若恐好名而不為，則非臣之所敢知也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty fears loving name and will not act, that is not what your servant dares know.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing name-seeking was not his concern.

sentences.zh: 陛下倘奮乾剛，明聽斷，則有英睿之名；

translations.literal: If Your Majesty rouses dry firmness and clear listening and deciding, then there is the name of heroic discernment;
translations.idiomatic: Resolve brings discerning rule;

sentences.zh: 行威令，懾奸宄，則有神武之名；

translations.literal: execute awe orders and cow traitors, then there is the name of divine martial prowess;
translations.idiomatic: awe orders bring martial renown;

sentences.zh: 斥奢汰，革風俗，則有崇儉之名；

translations.literal: reject luxury and reform customs, then there is the name of exalting frugality;
translations.idiomatic: frugality brings thrift renown;

sentences.zh: 澄冗濫，輕會斂，則有廣愛之名；

translations.literal: clarify redundancy and lighten levies, then there is the name of broad love;
translations.idiomatic: cutting levies brings humane renown;

sentences.zh: 悅亮直，惡巧媚，則有納諫之名；

translations.literal: delight in straight brightness and hate crafty flattery, then there is the name of accepting remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: welcoming blunt counsel brings remonstrance renown;

sentences.zh: 務咨詢，達壅蔽，則有勤政之名；

translations.literal: attend to consultation and penetrate obstruction, then there is the name of diligent government;
translations.idiomatic: consultation brings diligent-government renown;

sentences.zh: 責功實，抑偷幸，則有求治之名。

translations.literal: demand real merit and suppress lucky opportunism, then there is the name of seeking order.
translations.idiomatic: merit and punishing luck bring seeking-order renown.

sentences.zh: 今皆非之而不為，則天下何所望乎？

translations.literal: Now all are rejected and not done—then what does the realm hope for?
translations.idiomatic: Rejecting all leaves the realm hopeless.

sentences.zh: 抑又聖賢之道曰名教，忠誼之訓曰名節，群臣諸儒所以尊輔朝廷，紀綱人倫之大本也。

translations.literal: Moreover the way of sages and worthies is called name-teaching; the instruction of loyalty and righteousness is called name-integrity—what ministers and scholars use to honor and assist the court, the great root of regulating human relations.
translations.idiomatic: Name-teaching and name-integrity underpinned court and society.

sentences.zh: 陛下從而非之，則教化微，節義廢，無恥之徒爭進，而勸沮之方不行矣，豈聖人率下之意耶。”

translations.literal: If Your Majesty follows and rejects them, then teaching is slight, integrity abandoned, shameless men vie to advance and methods of encouragement and restraint cannot proceed—is this the sage's intent in leading those below?"
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty follows and rejects them, then teaching is slight, integrity abandoned, shameless men vie to advance and methods of encouragement and restraint cannot proceed—is this the sage's intent in leading those below?"

sentences.zh: 時邊奏契丹修天德城及多葺堡砦。

translations.literal: At the time border reports said Khitan repaired Tiande city and repaired many forts.
translations.idiomatic: Border reports said Khitan repaired Tiande and many forts.

sentences.zh: 況意其蓄奸謀，乃上疏曰：“朝廷予契丹金帛歲五十萬，朘削生民，輸將道路，疲弊之勢，漸不可久。

translations.literal: Kuang thought they stored treacherous plots and memorialized: "The court grants Khitan fifty thousand strings of gold and silk yearly, scraping the living people, transporting on roads—the weary trend gradually cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang thought they stored treacherous plots and memorialized: "The court grants Khitan fifty thousand strings of gold and silk yearly, scraping the living people, transporting on roads—the weary trend gradually cannot last long.

sentences.zh: 而近西羌通款，歲又予二十萬，設或復肆貪瀆，再有規求，朝廷尚可從乎？

translations.literal: Recently western Qiang made peace and yearly another twenty thousand is granted—suppose they again act greedy and have further demands, can the court still follow?
translations.idiomatic: Another twenty thousand to western Qiang—what if demands grew?

sentences.zh: 臣至愚，不當大責，每念至此，則惋嘆不已。

translations.literal: Your servant is most foolish and should not bear great responsibility; each time I think to here I sigh and lament without end.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed at the burden.

sentences.zh: 矧兩府大臣，皆宗廟社稷、天下生民所望而系安危者，豈不為陛下思之哉？

translations.literal: Moreover two-bureau chief ministers are those the altars of soil and grain and living people of the realm look to and on whom safety and danger hang—should they not think for Your Majesty?
translations.idiomatic: Chief ministers should bear the realm's safety.

sentences.zh: 每旦垂拱之對，不過目前政事數條而已，非陛下所以待輔臣，非輔臣所以憂朝廷之意也。

translations.literal: Each dawn's audience at drooping palisades is only a few current government items—not how Your Majesty should treat assisting ministers, not how assisting ministers should worry for the court.
translations.idiomatic: Morning audiences covered trivia, not grand strategy.

sentences.zh: 有唐故事，肅宗以天下未乂，除正衙奏事外，別開延英以詢訪宰相，蓋旁無侍衛，獻可替否，曲盡討論。

translations.literal: Tang had the story: Suzong because the realm was not pacified, besides regular court memorials, separately opened Yanying to inquire of chief ministers—there were no attendants at side, presenting approval or rejection, bending and fully discussing.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Suzong used Yanying sessions for frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 今北敵桀慢，而河朔將佐之良愚，中兵之善窳，道路之夷險，城壘之堅弊，軍政之是否，財糧之多少，在兩府輔臣，實未有知之者。

translations.literal: Now northern enemies are arrogant while Hebei generals' good and bad, central troops' sound and rotten, roads' level and rugged, ramparts' solid and broken, military government's yes and no, wealth and grain's how much—the two-bureau assisting ministers truly do not yet know.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers did not know frontier realities.

sentences.zh: 萬一變發所忽，制由中出，少有差跌，則事不測矣。

translations.literal: If by chance change erupts from what was neglected and control comes from within with slight error, then affairs are immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: Surprise crises from ignorance were immeasurable.

sentences.zh: 如前歲蕭英、劉六符始來，和議未決，中外惶擾，不知為計，此臣所目睹也。

translations.literal: As before when Xiao Ying and Liu Liufu first came and peace was undecided, inside and outside were alarmed not knowing what plan—this your servant witnessed with eyes.
translations.idiomatic: He had seen panic during Xiao Ying's mission.

sentences.zh: 和議既定，又復恬然若無事者，是豈得為安哉。

translations.literal: When peace was fixed they again were tranquil as if no affair—how could that be called secure?
translations.idiomatic: Peace brought false calm.

sentences.zh: 願因燕閑，召執政大臣於便殿，從容賜坐，訪逮時政，專以慮患為急。

translations.literal: I wish at leisure banquets to summon governing chief ministers in the side hall, calmly grant seats, inquire on current government, specializing in considering worry as urgent.
translations.idiomatic: He urged side-hall talks focused on peril.

sentences.zh: 則人人惟恐不知以誤應對，事事惟恐不集以孤聖懷，旦夕憂思，不敢少懈，同心協力，必有所為。

translations.literal: Then each man fears not knowing and errs in response; each affair fears not gathering and isolates sagely intent; day and night worry thinking, not daring slight slackening, same heart same strength, must have action.
translations.idiomatic: That would force informed, urgent counsel.

sentences.zh: 今不以此為務，而日以委瑣之事，更相辯對，議者羞之。

translations.literal: Now not taking this as task but daily on trifling affairs mutually arguing—speakers are ashamed.
translations.idiomatic: Instead they bickered over trifles.

sentences.zh: 臣叨備近列，實系朝廷休戚，惟陛下不以人廢言。”

translations.literal: Your servant occupies near rank, truly tied to court weal and woe—only Your Majesty do not reject words because of the man."
translations.idiomatic: Your servant occupies near rank, truly tied to court weal and woe—only Your Majesty do not reject words because of the man."

sentences.zh: 尋為陜西宣撫副使，還領三班院。

translations.literal: Soon made Shaanxi pacification deputy commissioner; on return headed the Three Ranks Court.
translations.idiomatic: He became Shaanxi deputy pacification commissioner, then headed Three Ranks.

sentences.zh: 保州雲翼軍殺州吏據城叛，詔況處置之。

translations.literal: Baozhou Cloud Wing Army killed prefecture clerks and held the city in revolt; an edict ordered Kuang to handle it.
translations.idiomatic: Cloud Wing mutiny at Baozhou was assigned to Kuang.

sentences.zh: 既而除龍圖閣直學士、知成德軍。

translations.literal: Before long made Dragon Hall straight academician and Chengde Army prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Dragon Hall straight academician and Chengde prefect.

sentences.zh: 況督諸將攻，以敕榜招降叛卒二千餘人，坑其構逆者四百二十九人，以功遷起居舍人。

translations.literal: Kuang supervised generals in attack; with edict placard summoned surrender of more than two thousand rebel soldiers, buried alive four hundred twenty-nine who plotted rebellion; for merit promoted Drafting Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He suppressed the mutiny, buried plotters, and was promoted.

sentences.zh: 徙秦州。

translations.literal: Moved to Qin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Moved to Qin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 丁父憂，詔起復，固辭。

translations.literal: Father mourning; edict ordered mourning leave interrupted; he firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: Father mourning: he refused interrupted mourning.

sentences.zh: 又遣內侍持手敕起之，不得已，乞歸葬陽翟。

translations.literal: Again sent inner attendant with handwritten edict to raise him; having no way out he begged return burial at Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: An inner attendant's edict sent him to bury his father at Yangzhai.

sentences.zh: 既葬，托邊事求見，泣請終制，仁宗惻然許之。

translations.literal: After burial he pleaded border affairs to see the emperor, weeping to request full mourning; Renzong compassionately permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He wept for full mourning and Renzong granted it.

sentences.zh: 帥臣得終喪自況始。

translations.literal: Commanders obtaining full mourning began with Kuang.
translations.idiomatic: Commanders' full mourning began with Kuang.

sentences.zh: 服除，以樞密直學士、尚書禮部郎中知渭州。

translations.literal: After mourning ended as Military Affairs straight academician and War Section director governing Wei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning, Military Affairs straight academician and Wei prefect.

sentences.zh: 遷右諫議大夫、知成都府。

translations.literal: Promoted Right Remonstrance Censor and Chengdu prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Right Remonstrance Censor and Chengdu prefect.

sentences.zh: 蜀自李順、王均再亂，人心易搖，守得便宜決事，多擅殺以為威，雖小罪，猶並妻子徙出蜀，至有流離死道路者。

translations.literal: Shu since Li Shun and Wang Jun twice rebelled, people's hearts easily shaken; prefects getting expedient decision often killed excessively for awe—even small crimes still exiled wives and children from Shu, even to wandering death on roads.
translations.idiomatic: Shu prefects exiled families harshly after Li Shun and Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 況至，拊循教誨，非有甚惡不使遷，蜀人尤愛之。

translations.literal: When Kuang arrived he soothed and taught; unless very wicked he did not make them move—Shu people especially loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang soothed Shu and rarely exiled people.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，召為御史中丞。

translations.literal: Promoted Supervising Censor; summoned as Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Censor, then Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 既至，權三司使，加龍圖閣學士、翰林學士。

translations.literal: On arrival acting Three Departments commissioner, added Dragon Hall academician and Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Three Departments commissioner, Dragon Hall and Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 況鉤考財賦，盡知其出入，乃約《景德會計錄》，以今財賦所入，多於景德，而歲之所出，又多於所入。

translations.literal: Kuang audited wealth and fully knew receipts and disbursements; then approximated 《Jingde Accounting Records》, finding present revenue in more than Jingde while yearly outflow also more than inflow.
translations.idiomatic: Auditing finances he found spending exceeded Jingde-era income.

sentences.zh: 因著《皇祐會計錄》上之。

translations.literal: He therefore authored 《Huangyou Accounting Records》 and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted 《Huangyou Accounting Records》.

sentences.zh: 以禮部侍郎為三司使。

translations.literal: As Vice Rites Minister he was Three Departments commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Rites Minister and Three Departments commissioner.

sentences.zh: 至和元年，擢樞密副使，遂為樞密使。

translations.literal: In Zhihe year one promoted Military Affairs vice commissioner, then Military Affairs commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihe year one he became Military Affairs commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以疾，罷為尚書右丞、觀文殿學士兼翰林侍讀學士，提舉景靈宮，遂以太子少傅致仕，卒。

translations.literal: Because of illness dismissed as Right Vice Director, Observant Culture academician with Hanlin Attendant Reader, overseer of Brilliant Numen Palace, then retired as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and died.
translations.idiomatic: Illness led to retirement as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and death.

sentences.zh: 贈太子太保，謚宣簡。

translations.literal: Posthumously made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Xuanjian.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent, posthumous Xuanjian.

sentences.zh: 況寬厚明敏，有文武材。

translations.literal: Kuang was generous, bright, and keen, with civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was generous, keen, and gifted in civil and military affairs.

sentences.zh: 與人若無不可，至其所守，人亦不能移也。

translations.literal: With people as if nothing impossible; yet what he guarded others also could not move.
translations.idiomatic: Affable yet immovable in principle.

sentences.zh: 其論天下事甚多，至並樞密院於中書以一政本，日輪兩制館閣官一員於便殿備訪問，以錫慶院廣太學，興鎮戎軍、原渭等州營田，汰諸路宣毅、廣捷等冗軍，策元昊勢屈納款，必令盡還延州侵地，毋過許歲幣，並入中青鹽，請戮陜西陷歿主將隨行親兵。

translations.literal: His discussions of realm affairs were many—to merge Military Affairs into the Central Secretariat for one government root, daily rotate one two-rankings or pavilion academician at the side hall for inquiry, use Xiqing Court to expand the Imperial University, open military colonies at Zhenrong Army and Yuan and Wei, cut redundant Xuanyi and Guangjie troops on circuits, strategize that when Yuan Hao's power bent he would offer peace and must fully return Yan Prefecture seized land, not over-grant yearly gifts, merge central Shaanxi salt, request executing Shaanxi fallen commanders' accompanying kin.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed merging bureaus, frontier colonies, troop cuts, and hard peace terms with Yuan Hao.

sentences.zh: 其論甚偉，然不盡行也。

translations.literal: The discussions were very grand, yet not fully carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Grand plans were only partly enacted.

sentences.zh: 有奏議二十卷。

translations.literal: He had twenty juan of memorials.
translations.idiomatic: He left twenty juan of memorials.

sentences.zh: 始，契丹寇澶州，略得數百人，以屬其父延昭。

translations.literal: At first when Khitan raided Chanzhou they captured several hundred men and gave them to his father Yanzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan captives were given to his father Yanzhao at Chanzhou.

sentences.zh: 延昭哀之，悉縱去，因自脫歸中國。

translations.literal: Yanzhao pitied them and all released them; thereby he himself escaped back to China.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao released them and escaped south.

sentences.zh: 延昭生八男，子多知名，況長子也。

translations.literal: Yanzhao had eight sons; sons were mostly known; Kuang was the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhao's eight sons were known; Kuang was eldest.

sentences.zh: 保州之役，況坑殺降卒數百人，朝廷壯其決，後大用之。

translations.literal: In the Baozhou affair Kuang buried alive several hundred surrendered soldiers; the court admired his decisiveness and later greatly used him.
translations.idiomatic: Baozhou mass burial won court trust.

sentences.zh: 然卒無子，以兄子為後。

translations.literal: Yet in the end he had no son and took his brother's son as heir.
translations.idiomatic: Childless, he adopted his brother's son.

sentences.zh: 論曰：時治平而文德用，則士之負藝者致位政府，宜矣。

translations.literal: The discourse says: When the age was orderly and civil virtue was employed, then scholars bearing arts reaching government posts—it was fitting.
translations.idiomatic: The discourse says civil times rightly elevated literati to power.

sentences.zh: 李諮、程戡曉暢吏事。

translations.literal: Li Zi and Cheng Kan were clear in clerical affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zi and Cheng Kan knew administration.

sentences.zh: 諮變茶法，雖浮議動搖，乍行乍止，卒無能易其說；

translations.literal: Zi changed tea law; though floating debate shook it, now running now stopping, in the end none could change his argument;
translations.idiomatic: Zi's tea reform survived debate;

sentences.zh: 戡任邊寄，守以安靜，非必智謀，抑所遇之時耳。

translations.literal: Kan held frontier trust, guarding with quiet— not necessarily wisdom and stratagem, perhaps also the times he met.
translations.idiomatic: Kan kept the frontier quiet by circumstance as much as genius.

sentences.zh: 嶠尚莊、老，以善著稱。

translations.literal: Jiao honored Zhuangzi and Laozi and was famed for goodness.
translations.idiomatic: Jiao honored Zhuangzi and Laozi and was known for virtue.

sentences.zh: 張觀、丁度、孫抃，世推其德性淳易，而盛度每為寮友猜憚，心跡固何如也。

translations.literal: Zhang Guan, Ding Du, and Sun Bian—the age praised their virtue as pure and easy, while Sheng Du was often suspected and feared by colleagues—what indeed were mind and traces?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guan, Ding Du, and Sun Bian were praised as plain and virtuous; Sheng Du was feared by colleagues—what were his true motives?

sentences.zh: 戩明偉宏放，亦一時之俊。

translations.literal: Jian was bright, grand, and expansive—also a talent of the time.
translations.idiomatic: Jian too was a brilliant talent of the age.

sentences.zh: 堯臣論議鏗鏗，正誼而不謀利，其最優乎。

translations.literal: Yaochen's discourse rang clear, upright in principle and not scheming profit—was he the best?
translations.idiomatic: Yaochen's ringing discourse was upright and unprofitable—perhaps the best.

sentences.zh: 鎬堅正寡合，馭軍嚴，臨事果，其安撫河東邊塞，後來父老道其舉動措置，輒嗟嘆追思。

translations.literal: Gao was upright and solitary, commanding troops strictly, decisive in affairs; his pacification of Hedong border garrisons—later elders speaking of his measures always sighed and recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was upright and strict; elders long recalled his Hedong frontier measures.

sentences.zh: 況有文武才略，言事精暢，然欲懲兵驕，乃坑降卒，弗忌陰禍，惜哉！

translations.literal: Kuang had civil and military talent and strategy, memorials precise and fluent; yet wishing to punish soldier arrogance he buried surrendered troops, not fearing hidden calamity—pity!
translations.idiomatic: Kuang was gifted and eloquent, yet burying surrendered troops to punish arrogance ignored hidden harm—pity.
